!.name: Factorial
!.description: Computes the factorial of a non-negative integer; for other reals it uses the gamma function, giving Γ(x+1).

examples.comment: A non-integer gives the gamma function's value Γ(1.5)

%.name: Percent
%.description: Computes y percent of x, i.e. x·y/100. Units on x carry over to the result.
%.stack: x y → x·y/100; x_unit y → (x·y/100)_unit; 'symb' y → '%(symb,y)'

28s.description: Computes y percent of x, that is x·y/100.

%CH.name: Percent change
%CH.description: Computes the percentage change going from x to y, i.e. 100·(y-x)/x; a decrease gives a negative result.

examples.comment: From 50 to 60 is a rise of 20 percent

%T.name: Percent of total
%T.description: Computes what percentage y is of the total x, i.e. 100·y/x.

'.description: Quote delimiter: a name or expression written between single quotes is pushed as an object rather than evaluated.
'.skip: a delimiter of command-line and program source, not a command that runs on its own

*.name: Multiply
*.description: Multiplies two objects: numbers, binary integers, units (combining their dimensions), algebraics, and arrays including matrix by matrix or matrix by vector products.

28s.description: Multiplies two objects: numbers, binary integers, algebraics, and arrays including matrix by matrix or matrix by vector products.

*H.name: Multiply height
*H.description: Multiplies the height of the plot range by a factor, so the vertical extent in PPAR grows or shrinks; the y value at the display's centre row stays where it is.

examples.comment: The y range -3.1 to 3.2 doubles to -6.2 to 6.4; 0, at the centre row, stays put

*W.name: Multiply width
*W.description: Multiplies the width of the plot range by a factor, keeping it centred, so the horizontal extent in PPAR grows or shrinks.

examples.comment: The x range -6.5 to 6.5 doubles to -13 to 13; the y range stays

+.name: Add
+.description: Adds two objects: numbers, binary integers, arrays of equal size, compatible unit objects and algebraics. With strings it concatenates, and with a list it appends or joins lists.

28s.description: Adds two objects: numbers, binary integers, arrays of equal size and algebraics. With strings it concatenates, and with a list it appends or joins lists.

-.name: Subtract
-.description: Subtracts level 1 from level 2 for reals, complex numbers, binary integers, same-size arrays, compatible units and algebraics.
-.stack: x y → x-y; z1 z2 → z1-z2; 'symb1' 'symb2' → 'symb1-symb2'

28s.description: Subtracts level 1 from level 2 for reals, complex numbers, binary integers, same-size arrays and algebraics.
28s.stack: x y → x-y; z1 z2 → z1-z2; 'symb1' 'symb2' → 'symb1-symb2'

/.name: Divide
/.description: Divides level 2 by level 1 for numbers, binary integers, units and algebraics; with a matrix in level 1 it solves the linear system for the array in level 2.

examples.comment: Solves the linear system: the matrix times the result gives [ 5 6 ]

28s.description: Divides level 2 by level 1 for numbers, binary integers and algebraics; with a matrix in level 1 it solves the linear system for the array in level 2.

;.description: Separator token for function arguments and list items in algebraic entry; it does no work as a stand-alone command.
;.skip: a syntax separator, not a command that does anything on its own

<.name: Less than
<.description: Compares level 2 against level 1 and pushes 1 if it is smaller, else 0; accepts reals, binary integers, strings (compared by character code) and units of compatible dimension, and yields a symbolic comparison for names or algebraics.

examples.comment: Units are compared after conversion: 1 m is longer than 50 cm

28s.description: Compares level 2 against level 1 and pushes 1 if it is smaller, else 0; accepts reals, binary integers and strings (compared by character code), and yields a symbolic comparison for names or algebraics.

=.name: Equation
=.description: Joins two objects into an equation with the first as left side and the second as right side. Evaluating the equation numerically gives the difference of the two sides.

==.name: Equal (test)
==.description: Tests two objects for equality, returning 1 or 0; reals and complex numbers compare by value, other objects by type and content. When a name or algebraic is involved it returns a symbolic comparison instead.

>.name: Greater than
>.description: Compares level 2 against level 1 and pushes 1 if it is larger, else 0; accepts reals, binary integers, strings and compatible units, and yields a symbolic comparison for names or algebraics.

28s.description: Compares level 2 against level 1 and pushes 1 if it is larger, else 0; accepts reals, binary integers and strings (compared by character code), and yields a symbolic comparison for names or algebraics.

?.name: Undefined
?.description: Puts the undefined symbol on the stack, the value the CAS uses for a result that cannot be determined.

ABCUV.name: Polynomial Bézout equation
ABCUV.description: Solves the polynomial Bezout equation a*u+b*v=c for u and v, given polynomials a, b and c.

examples.comment: Finds u and v with (X^2+1)*u+(X-1)*v=1

ABORT.description: Stops the running program at the point where it stands. The program cannot be resumed.

ABS.name: Absolute value
ABS.description: Gives the size of a value: a real without its sign, a complex number's modulus, or an array's Frobenius (Euclidean) length. Units are kept, and symbolic arguments give a symbolic result.
ABS.stack: x → |x|; z → x; [array] → x; x_unit → x_unit; 'symb' → 'ABS(symb)'

28s.description: Gives the size of a value: a real without its sign, a complex number's modulus, or an array's Frobenius (Euclidean) length. Symbolic arguments give a symbolic result.

ACK.name: Acknowledge alarm
ACK.description: Acknowledges the oldest past-due appointment alarm, clearing it from the due list (and the alarm annunciator when none remain).

ACKALL.name: Acknowledge all alarms
ACKALL.description: Acknowledges every past-due appointment alarm at once, turning off the alarm annunciator; repeating alarms are rescheduled.

ACOS.name: Arc cosine
ACOS.description: Arc cosine, giving the angle in the current angle mode. Reals outside -1 to 1 produce a complex result.
ACOS.stack: x → acos x; z → acos z; 'symb' → 'ACOS(symb)'

ACOS2S.name: Arc cosine to arc sine
ACOS2S.description: Rewrites an expression so that every arccosine in it becomes pi/2 minus the arcsine of the same argument.

ACOSH.name: Inverse hyperbolic cosine
ACOSH.description: Computes the inverse hyperbolic cosine of a real or complex argument; reals below 1 give a complex result.
ACOSH.stack: x → acosh x; z → acosh z; 'symb' → 'ACOSH(symb)'

ADD.description: Adds two lists element by element, or adds one object to each item of a list; unlike +, it never concatenates lists.

ADDTMOD.name: Add modulo
ADDTMOD.description: Adds two expressions or integers and reduces the result modulo the current CAS modulus.

examples.comment: The sum X^2+12*X+9 reduces modulo 7 to X^2-2*X+2
Modulo 7: 5 plus 4 gives 2

ADDTOREAL.name: Add to real assumptions
ADDTOREAL.description: Declares a variable as real for the CAS by adding its name to the REALASSUME list, so simplifications may assume it has no imaginary part.

ALGB.name: Algebra menu
ALGB.description: Opens the CAS menu of algebra commands (expand, factor, substitute, and so on).

ALOG.name: Common antilogarithm
ALOG.description: Raises 10 to the given power, the inverse of LOG.

AMORT.name: Amortize
AMORT.description: Amortizes the next n payments of a loan described by the stored TVM variables, returning the principal and interest paid over those payments and the remaining balance.

examples.comment: First 12 monthly payments of 200 on 10000 at 6% a year: principal, interest, balance

AND.description: Bitwise AND of two binary integers; for reals it is a logical AND treating any non-zero value as true and returning 1 or 0. Symbolic arguments give a symbolic expression.

examples.comment: Binary 1100 AND 1010 gives 1000

ANIMATE.description: Shows a series of grobs one after another on the display as an animation, with optional frame delay, position and repeat count.
ANIMATE.stack: grob1 ... grobn n →; grob1 ... grobn { n { #x #y } delay rep } →
ANIMATE.skip: animates on the screen until a key is pressed

ANS.name: Answer
ANS.description: Recalls an earlier result from the algebraic-mode history; the argument says how many entries back to go.
ANS.skip: reads the algebraic-mode history, which RPN-mode examples do not build

APEEK.name: Address peek
APEEK.description: Reads the five-nibble address stored in memory at the given address and returns it as a binary integer; needs library 256 attached.

APPLY.description: Builds a function-call expression from a function name and a list of arguments, without evaluating the function; mainly used by user-defined functions to return symbolic results.

ARC.description: Draws an arc of a circle in the graphics picture from a centre, radius and start and end angles in the current angle mode.
ARC.skip: draws into the graphics picture and returns nothing to the stack

ARCHIVE.description: Makes a backup copy of the whole HOME directory, either as a backup object in a port (:n:name) or sent over Kermit (:IO:name).

examples.comment: Backs up HOME to port 0 under the name BK; PVARS then lists it

ARG.name: Argument
ARG.description: Gives the angle of a complex value in polar form, measured from the positive real axis in the current angle mode; a real gives 0 or a half turn depending on its sign.

ARIT.name: Arithmetic menu
ARIT.description: Opens the CAS menu of arithmetic commands for integers, polynomials and modular arithmetic.

ARM→.description: Low-level command for ARM-based models that converts ARM machine code; it has no use on the Saturn-only 49G. Part of the development library.

ARRY→.name: Array to stack
ARRY→.description: Splits an array into its elements in row order, followed by a list of its dimensions. Superseded by OBJ→ but still accepted.

28s.description: Splits an array into its elements in row order, followed by a list of its dimensions. →ARRY builds the array again.

ASIN.name: Arc sine
ASIN.description: Arc sine, giving the angle in the current angle mode. Reals outside -1 to 1 produce a complex result.
ASIN.stack: x → asin x; z → asin z; 'symb' → 'ASIN(symb)'

ASIN2C.name: Arc sine to arc cosine
ASIN2C.description: Rewrites an expression so that every arcsine in it becomes pi/2 minus the arccosine of the same argument.

ASIN2T.name: Arc sine to arc tangent
ASIN2T.description: Replaces each arc sine in an expression by an equivalent arc tangent, using asin(x) = atan(x/√(1-x²)).

ASINH.name: Inverse hyperbolic sine
ASINH.description: Computes the inverse hyperbolic sine (area sine) of a real or complex argument.
ASINH.stack: x → asinh x; z → asinh z; 'symb' → 'ASINH(symb)'

ASM.name: Assemble
ASM.description: Assembles a string of MASD source (Saturn assembler or System RPL) into the object it describes. On a syntax error it leaves error information for ER. Part of the development library.

ASM2.description: Internal entry of the MASD assembler library; not meant for direct use.

ASM→.name: Disassemble
ASM→.description: Disassembles a machine-code object into a string of Saturn assembler source. Part of the development library.
ASM→.skip: needs a machine-code object, which only the assembler can create; low-level development tool

ASN.name: Assign key
ASN.description: Assigns an object to a key for USER mode; the key is given as row-column.plane (e.g. 11.1), and the SKEY object restores the key's built-in function.

examples.comment: Puts « 1 » on key 11 (row 1, column 1, unshifted); RCLKEYS shows it

ASR.name: Arithmetic shift right
ASR.description: Arithmetic right shift: moves every bit of a binary integer down one position but keeps the top bit (as set by the word size) as it was, so a two's-complement sign survives.

examples.comment: The top bit stays set as the other bits move down

ASSUME.description: Records an assumption about a variable for the CAS, such as a sign condition; kept from the HP 40G CAS and of limited effect on the 49G.
ASSUME.skip: on the 49G it does not return for a condition such as 'X>0' when run headless

ATAN.name: Arc tangent
ATAN.description: Arc tangent, giving the angle in the current angle mode, for reals, complex numbers and algebraics.
ATAN.stack: x → atan x; z → atan z; 'symb' → 'ATAN(symb)'

ATAN2S.name: Arc tangent to arc sine
ATAN2S.description: Replaces each arc tangent in an expression by an equivalent arc sine, using atan(x) = asin(x/√(x²+1)).

ATANH.name: Inverse hyperbolic tangent
ATANH.description: Computes the inverse hyperbolic tangent; reals outside -1..1 produce a complex result, while exactly ±1 is an infinite-result error.
ATANH.stack: x → atanh x; z → atanh z; 'symb' → 'ATANH(symb)'

ATICK.name: Axes tick marks
ATICK.description: Sets the spacing of axis tick marks in PPAR: a real value counts user units while a binary integer counts pixels, and a two-element list sets x and y separately.

ATTACH.name: Attach library
ATTACH.description: Attaches a library, given by number or :port:number, to the current directory so its commands become available.
ATTACH.skip: needs a library object stored in a port

AUGMENT.description: Appends an element or a block to a list, vector or matrix, joining them into one larger object.

AUTO.name: Autoscale
AUTO.description: Picks a vertical plot range automatically by sampling the current equation over the horizontal range, updating PPAR; useful before DRAW when the y values are unknown.

AXES.description: Sets the point where the plot axes cross, stored in PPAR as a complex coordinate in user units.

AXL.name: Array to list
AXL.description: Converts between arrays and lists: an array becomes a list (of lists for a matrix), and a list becomes the corresponding array.

AXM.name: Array to symbolic matrix
AXM.description: Converts a numeric array into a symbolic matrix, turning real entries into exact values where possible.

AXQ.name: Matrix to quadratic form
AXQ.description: Turns a square matrix and a vector of variables into the quadratic form they define, leaving the variable vector on level 1; the inverse of QXA.

A→.name: Address to object
A→.description: Returns the object found at a memory address given as a binary integer; needs library 256 attached.

A→H.name: Address to hex
A→H.description: Converts an address given as a binary integer to its five-digit hexadecimal string in nibble order (least significant digit first); needs library 256 attached.

examples.comment: The five digits come back in reverse order

BAR.name: Bar plot type
BAR.description: Selects the bar plot type, which draws one bar per value of a ΣDAT column.

BARPLOT.name: Draw bar plot
BARPLOT.description: Draws a bar chart of a column of ΣDAT into the graphics picture.
BARPLOT.skip: draws into the graphics picture and returns nothing to the stack

BASIS.description: Extracts a basis of the vector subspace spanned by a list of vectors.

BAUD.name: Baud rate
BAUD.description: Sets the serial port speed (1200, 2400, 4800 or 9600 baud) in IOPAR.

examples.comment: The baud rate is the first element of IOPAR

BEEP.description: Sounds a tone of the given frequency in hertz for the given duration in seconds, unless beeping has been turned off with flag -56.
BEEP.skip: produces a sound and returns nothing to the stack

28s.description: Sounds a tone of the given frequency in hertz for the given duration in seconds, unless flag 51 is set to silence the beeper.

BESTFIT.name: Best-fitting model
BESTFIT.description: Tries all four regression models on the current ΣDAT columns and keeps the one whose correlation has the largest magnitude, storing the model and its coefficients in ΣPAR.

examples.comment: Data that triple at each step fit an exponential model best

BIN.name: Binary mode
BIN.description: Selects base 2 for displaying binary integers.

examples.comment: Decimal 12 is 1100 in binary
Hexadecimal FF is eight ones in binary

BINS.name: Sort into frequency bins
BINS.description: Sorts the independent column of ΣDAT into a number of equal-width bins starting at a minimum value; returns the count per bin as a one-column matrix and the counts below and above the range as a vector.

examples.comment: Two bins of width 2 from 0: counts per bin, then counts below and above

BLANK.name: Blank graphics object
BLANK.description: Creates an empty graphics object of the given width and height in pixels, ready to be drawn into or combined with GOR and GXOR.

BOX.description: Draws a rectangle in the graphics picture whose opposite corners are the two given points.
BOX.skip: draws into the graphics picture and returns nothing to the stack

BUFLEN.name: Buffer length
BUFLEN.description: Returns the number of characters waiting in the serial input buffer and 1, or 0 if a framing or overrun error occurred.

BYTES.name: Byte size
BYTES.description: Returns a binary checksum of an object and its size in bytes; given a name, it measures the variable's contents.

BetaTesting.description: Internal command of the development library; not meant for direct use.

B→R.name: Binary to real
B→R.description: Converts a binary integer to the equivalent real number; very large binary integers lose precision since reals keep 12 digits.

examples.comment: Hexadecimal FF is 255
Binary 101 is 5

C2P.name: Cycles to permutation
C2P.description: Converts a permutation written as a list of cycles into the list of images of 1..n.

examples.comment: The cycles (1 3) and (2 4) give the images 3, 4, 1, 2

CASCFG.name: Reset CAS configuration
CASCFG.description: Puts the CAS settings back to their defaults (exact mode, X as current variable, default modulus and the related flags).
CASCFG.skip: resets the CAS configuration only; nothing to show on the stack

CASCMD.name: CAS command browser
CASCMD.description: Opens a browser listing every CAS command, from which one can be picked and placed on the command line.

CASE.description: Opens a multi-way branch CASE test1 THEN clause1 END test2 THEN clause2 END … [default] END: the first test that yields a nonzero value has its clause run, the rest are skipped, and an optional default clause runs when none matches. Only valid inside programs.

examples.run: « CASE DUP 1. == THEN "A" END DUP 2. == THEN "B" END END » EVAL
examples.comment: The test for 1 fails, the test for 2 passes and pushes B

CD→.name: Code object to hex string
CD→.description: Returns the body of a code object as a string of hexadecimal digits, the inverse of →CD; needs library 256 attached.

CEIL.name: Ceiling
CEIL.description: Rounds a real number up to the nearest integer not less than it.

examples.comment: A negative number rounds up towards zero

28s.description: Rounds a real number up to the nearest integer not less than it.

CENTR.name: Center plot
CENTR.description: Moves the plot window so that the given point lies at its center, keeping the current width and height. A real argument is taken as the x coordinate with y 0.

28s.description: Moves the plot window so that the given point lies at its centre, keeping the current width and height.

CF.name: Clear flag
CF.description: Clears a flag; positive numbers address user flags 1 to 64, negative numbers the system flags.

examples.comment: Sets flag 3, clears it, then tests it: 0 means clear

28s.description: Clears user flag n, from 1 to 64. Flags 31 to 64 control calculator settings such as the binary base and the beeper.

CHINREM.name: Chinese remainder (polynomials)
CHINREM.description: Applies the Chinese remainder theorem to two polynomial congruences, each given as a vector [expression modulus], and returns the combined congruence the same way.

CHOLESKY.description: Computes the Cholesky factor of a symmetric positive-definite matrix: the triangular matrix whose product with its transpose gives back the matrix.

CHOOSE.name: Choose box
CHOOSE.description: Displays a choose box with a title and a list of items, waits for a selection, and returns the chosen item with 1, or just 0 when cancelled. The start position selects the highlighted item.
CHOOSE.skip: waits for the user to pick from an interactive choose box

CHR.name: Character
CHR.description: Returns a one-character string for a character code from 0 to 255; the inverse of NUM.

CIRC.name: Compose permutations
CIRC.description: Composes two permutations given as lists of images, returning the permutation obtained by applying one after the other.

examples.comment: The two permutations are inverses, so the result is the identity

CKSM.name: Checksum type
CKSM.description: Chooses the Kermit block check type (1, 2 or 3) and stores it in IOPAR.

CLKADJ.name: Adjust system clock
CLKADJ.description: Moves the system clock forward (positive) or back (negative) by a number of ticks, 8192 ticks per second.

examples.comment: Moves the clock forward by one second (8192 ticks)
Moves the clock back by 2.5 seconds

CLLCD.name: Clear display
CLLCD.description: Blanks the stack area of the screen, leaving the status line and menu labels; typically used before a program writes its own output with DISP.
CLLCD.skip: clears the screen and returns nothing to the stack

28s.description: Blanks the whole display apart from the annunciators and sets the message flag, so the blank screen stays up after the program ends. Programs use it before writing their own output with DISP.

CLMF.name: Clear message flag
CLMF.description: Clears the message flag, which DRAW, DRWΣ, DRAX, PIXEL, DISP and CLLCD set, so the normal stack display comes back when the program ends.
CLMF.skip: changes only what the display shows after a program and returns nothing to the stack

CLOSEIO.name: Close I/O port
CLOSEIO.description: Closes the serial and infrared ports and discards any buffered input, saving power.
CLOSEIO.skip: talks over the serial or IR port

CLTEACH.name: Clear teaching examples
CLTEACH.description: Deletes the EXAMPLES directory, with everything in it, from HOME, undoing TEACH.

CLUSR.name: Clear user variables
CLUSR.description: Purges every variable and every empty subdirectory in the current directory.

CLVAR.name: Clear variables
CLVAR.description: Purges every variable stored in the directory you are in; it stops with an error at a subdirectory that is not empty.

CLΣ.name: Clear statistics data
CLΣ.description: Deletes the statistics data in ΣDAT so that the next Σ+ starts a fresh data set.

examples.comment: The old data is gone: only the new point 7 remains

CMPLX.name: Complex number menu
CMPLX.description: Opens the CAS menu of commands for complex numbers.

CNRM.name: Column norm
CNRM.description: Computes an array's one-norm, also called its column norm: the largest column total of absolute values; for a vector, every element's absolute value is added up.

COL+.name: Insert column
COL+.description: Inserts a vector as a new column at position n of a matrix, shifting the following columns right; n may be one past the last column to append. On a vector it inserts a number as element n.

examples.comment: Inserts [ 9 9 ] as the new column 1
Inserts the number 2 as element 2

COL-.name: Delete column
COL-.description: Removes column n from a matrix and returns the narrowed matrix together with the removed column as a vector. On a vector it removes and returns element n.

COLCT.name: Collect like terms
COLCT.description: Simplifies an expression by collecting like terms and combining numeric parts, putting it in a tidy order.

COLLECT.description: Gathers like terms of an algebraic expression and factors it over the integers, a lighter form of FACTOR that does not split factors with irrational roots.

COLΣ.name: Statistics columns
COLΣ.description: Chooses which columns of ΣDAT act as the independent and dependent variables for regression and plotting, storing them in ΣPAR.

examples.comment: Column 2 is the independent variable, column 1 the dependent one

COL→.name: Columns to matrix
COL→.description: Assembles a matrix from a count and that many column vectors on the stack, the first column deepest. With plain numbers it makes a row vector.

COMB.name: Combinations
COMB.description: Gives the number of ways to choose m out of n items when order does not matter: n!/(m!(n-m)!).

examples.comment: The number of five-card hands from a 52-card deck

28s.description: Gives the number of ways to choose m out of n items when order does not matter: n!/(m!(n-m)!).

COMP→.name: Composite to stack
COMP→.description: Splits a list, program or algebraic (any composite) into its elements followed by their count; needs library 256 attached.
COMP→.stack: {list} → obj1 ... objn n; prog → obj1 ... objn n

CON.name: Constant array
CON.description: Builds an array whose elements all equal a given value, either from a list of dimensions or by filling an existing array (or array variable) with that value.

COND.name: Condition number
COND.description: For a square matrix, gives its condition number based on the column (1-) norm, which measures how sensitive solving with it is to errors.

CONIC.name: Conic plot type
CONIC.description: Selects the conic plot type, which draws a second-degree equation in two variables such as a circle or ellipse.

CONJ.name: Conjugate
CONJ.description: Returns the complex conjugate by flipping the sign of the imaginary part, for a complex number or for every element of a complex array; real arguments come back unchanged.

CONLIB.name: Constants library
CONLIB.description: Opens the Constants Library browser for viewing physical constants and copying them to the stack.
CONLIB.skip: opens an interactive catalog that waits for keys

CONST.name: Constant value
CONST.description: Returns the value of a named physical constant from the Constants Library, with SI or English units by flag 60 and as a plain number if flag 61 is set.

examples.comment: NA is Avogadro's number
With flag 61 set the value has no units; g is standard gravity

CONSTANTS.description: Opens the CAS menu or selection list of symbolic constants such as e, i, π and infinity.
CONSTANTS.skip: opens a menu or a selection screen

CONT.name: Continue
CONT.description: Resumes a program that was suspended by HALT or by a single-step debug session, carrying on from the point where it stopped.
CONT.skip: needs a program halted interactively; with nothing halted it does nothing

CONVERT.description: Converts a unit object into the units of a second unit object, which must have compatible dimensions; temperatures convert as absolute values unless written as differences.

28s.description: Converts a real number from one unit to another, the units given as strings or names. It returns the converted number and the new unit string; both units must measure the same kind of quantity.

CORR.name: Correlation
CORR.description: Gives the correlation coefficient for the two ΣDAT columns that XCOL and YCOL choose.

28s.description: Returns the correlation coefficient between the two columns of ΣDAT chosen by COLΣ, columns 1 and 2 by default.

COS.name: Cosine
COS.description: Cosine of an angle in the current angle mode, for reals, complex numbers and algebraics.
COS.stack: x → cos x; z → cos z; 'symb' → 'COS(symb)'

COSH.name: Hyperbolic cosine
COSH.description: Computes the hyperbolic cosine of a real or complex argument; symbolic arguments give a symbolic result.
COSH.stack: x → cosh x; z → cosh z; 'symb' → 'COSH(symb)'

COV.name: Covariance
COV.description: Gives the sample covariance for the two ΣDAT columns that XCOL and YCOL choose.

CR.name: Carriage return
CR.description: Sends a carriage return and line feed to the printer, flushing its buffer.
CR.skip: prints to the infrared or serial printer

CRC.name: Cyclic redundancy check
CRC.description: Computes the cyclic redundancy check of the data in a string and returns it as a binary integer. Part of the development library.

CRDIR.name: Create directory
CRDIR.description: Makes a new, empty subdirectory in the current directory under the given name.

CRLIB.name: Create library
CRLIB.description: Builds a library object from the variables of the current directory, steered by control variables such as $ROMID, $TITLE, $CONFIG, $VISIBLE and $HIDDEN. Part of the development library.
CRLIB.skip: needs a prepared directory with library control variables; development tool

CROSS.name: Cross product
CROSS.description: Computes the vector (cross) product of two three-element vectors, giving a vector perpendicular to both.

CSWP.name: Column swap
CSWP.description: Exchanges two columns of a matrix, or two elements of a vector, given their indices.

CURL.description: Computes the curl of a three-component vector field in three variables.

CYCLOTOMIC.description: Returns the n-th cyclotomic polynomial in the current variable, the monic polynomial whose roots are the primitive n-th roots of unity.

CYLIN.name: Cylindrical mode
CYLIN.description: Switches the coordinate mode to cylindrical (polar in two dimensions), so vectors and complex numbers are shown with an angle (sets flag -16, clears -15).

C→PX.name: Complex to pixel
C→PX.description: Converts a user-unit coordinate into the pixel position it falls on in the graphics picture, using the ranges in PPAR.

examples.comment: The origin falls on pixel 65, 32 of the default plot window
(-6.5,3.2), the plot window's upper-left point, is pixel 0, 0

C→R.name: Complex to real
C→R.description: Splits a complex number into two reals, the real part and then the imaginary part; a complex array gives two real arrays.

DARCY.name: Darcy friction factor
DARCY.description: Computes the Darcy-Weisbach friction factor for pipe flow from the relative roughness and the Reynolds number; it equals four times the Fanning factor.

examples.comment: Relative roughness 0.0001, Reynolds number 100000
Zero roughness at Reynolds number 1000 gives 64 divided by 1000

DATE.description: Returns the current date of the system clock as a real number, in MM.DDYYYY form or DD.MMYYYY when flag -42 is set.

examples.comment: 1.012030 is 1 January 2030 in MM.DDYYYY form

DATE+.name: Add days to date
DATE+.description: Adds a number of days (negative to go back) to a date and returns the resulting date.

examples.comment: 120 days after 15 July 1991 is 12 November 1991
One day before 1 March 2024 is 29 February, a leap year

DBUG.name: Debug
DBUG.description: Starts a program in suspended state so it can be stepped through one command at a time with the single-step keys, for debugging.
DBUG.skip: halts the program and waits for the user to single-step it

DDAYS.name: Days between dates
DDAYS.description: Counts the days from the first date to the second, negative when the second is earlier.

examples.comment: From 1 January to 15 July 1991, in MM.DDYYYY form
The second date is earlier, so the count is negative

DEC.name: Decimal mode
DEC.description: Selects base 10 for displaying binary integers.

examples.comment: Hexadecimal FF is 255 in decimal
Binary 101 is 5 in decimal

DECR.name: Decrement
DECR.description: Subtracts 1 from a variable holding a real number, stores it, and returns the new value.

DEDICACE.name: Dedication
DEDICACE.description: Hidden credit screen of the CAS that shows a dedication from its authors; it has no mathematical use.
DEDICACE.skip: displays a message on the screen

DEF.name: Define
DEF.description: Defines a variable or a user function from an equation written as 'name=expr' or 'name(args)=expr', like DEFINE; kept for HP 40G CAS compatibility.

examples.comment: Defines F(X)=X^2, then calls F with 3

DEFINE.description: Takes an equation name=expression and stores the right-hand expression in that variable; when the left side carries arguments, as in F(X)=..., it creates a user-defined function.

examples.comment: Defines the function F, then calls it with 3

DEG.name: Degrees mode
DEG.description: Selects degrees as the angle unit for trigonometric functions and polar displays.

DEGREE.description: Returns the degree of a polynomial in the CAS's current variable (VX, X by default) or, when that variable does not occur, in its first variable in alphabetical order.

examples.comment: Only the powers of X count, not those of Y

DELALARM.name: Delete alarm
DELALARM.description: Deletes the alarm with the given index from the alarm list, or every alarm when the index is 0.

examples.comment: Index 0 deletes every alarm, so FINDALARM then finds none

DELAY.description: Sets the pause in seconds between lines sent to the printer, kept in the PRTPAR variable.

examples.comment: The delay is the first element of PRTPAR

DELKEYS.name: Delete key assignments
DELKEYS.description: Clears the USER-mode assignment of one key, of a list of keys, or of all keys when given 0.

examples.comment: Removes the assignment on key 11 only; the one on key 12 stays

DEPND.name: Dependent variable
DEPND.description: Stores the name of the dependent plot variable in PPAR, the variable the plot treats as vertical.

DEPTH.description: Returns the number of objects currently on the stack.

DERIV.name: Derivative
DERIV.description: Differentiates an expression for a given variable; with a vector of variables it returns the vector of partial derivatives (the gradient).

DERVX.name: Derivative in the current variable
DERVX.description: Differentiates an expression in the current CAS variable (VX, normally X).

DESOLVE.name: Solve differential equation
DESOLVE.description: Attempts to solve some first-order ODEs for an unknown function, returning the solutions with integration constants such as cC0.

DET.name: Determinant
DET.description: Computes a square matrix's determinant by LU decomposition, so small rounding errors can appear in the result.

DETACH.name: Detach library
DETACH.description: Detaches a library, given by number or :port:number, from the current directory.

DGTIZ.name: Digitise
DGTIZ.description: Lets a program hand the plot to the user, usually after DRAW or DRWΣ: the cursor can be moved and coordinates put on the stack. Pressing ON lets the program go on.
DGTIZ.skip: waits for the user to pick points on the plot

DIAGMAP.name: Matrix function by diagonalization
DIAGMAP.description: Applies a function of the current variable to a diagonalizable matrix by diagonalizing it, applying the function to the eigenvalues, and transforming back.

examples.comment: Squares the eigenvalues of the matrix, 1 and 4

DIAG→.name: Vector to diagonal matrix
DIAG→.description: Creates a matrix of the given dimensions whose main diagonal holds the elements of a vector and whose other entries are zero.

DIFF.name: Calculus menu
DIFF.description: Opens the CAS menu of calculus commands (derivatives, integrals, limits, series, differential equations).

DIFFEQ.name: Differential equation plot type
DIFFEQ.description: Selects the differential-equation plot as the current plot type, which numerically integrates the equation in EQ and graphs the solution curve.

DIR.name: Directory
DIR.description: Begins the source form of a directory object, a sequence of names and their contents ended by END, as seen when a directory is transferred as text.
DIR.skip: a delimiter of directory source, not a command that runs on its own

DISP.name: Display
DISP.description: Shows an object on a chosen line of the display (1 at the top through 7), formatting non-strings first; programs use it for messages and status output.
DISP.skip: writes to the screen and returns nothing to the stack

28s.description: Shows an object on a chosen line of the display, 1 at the top through 4, with strings shown without quotes. It sets the message flag, so the output stays up after the program ends.

DISPXY.name: Display at pixel position
DISPXY.description: Shows an object on the screen at a given pixel position, using the font size selected by a number.
DISPXY.skip: draws on the screen and returns nothing to the stack

DISTRIB.name: Distribute
DISTRIB.description: Applies one step of distribution of multiplication over addition, letting an expression be expanded gradually.

DIV.name: Divergence
DIV.description: Computes the divergence of a vector field with respect to a vector of variables.

DIV2.name: Euclidean division
DIV2.description: Performs Euclidean division of two polynomials (or integers), returning the quotient and the remainder.

DIV2MOD.name: Euclidean division modulo
DIV2MOD.description: Performs Euclidean division of two polynomials or integers modulo the current CAS modulus, returning quotient and remainder.

examples.comment: Quotient X, remainder X+4, which is X+1 modulo 3
11 is 4 modulo 7, so 11 divided by 4 gives 1, remainder 0

DIVIS.name: Divisors
DIVIS.description: Lists all divisors of an integer, or of a polynomial.

DIVMOD.name: Divide modulo
DIVMOD.description: Divides the first expression or integer by the second in arithmetic modulo the current CAS modulus.

examples.comment: Modulo 7, so 3 times -3 gives 5

DIVPC.name: Division by increasing powers
DIVPC.description: Divides one expression by another as power series in the current variable, giving the quotient as a Taylor polynomial around 0 up to the requested degree.

examples.comment: 1/(1-X) as a series up to X^4

DO.description: Opens a post-tested loop DO body UNTIL test END: the body always runs at least once and repeats until the test clause leaves a nonzero value. Only valid inside programs.

examples.comment: Multiplies by 3 until the value is above 50: 3, 9, 27, 81

DOERR.name: Do error
DOERR.description: Raises an error on purpose: a string becomes a user error with that text as its message, a number or binary integer raises the built-in error with that code, and 0 aborts quietly like the ATTN key. Typically used in programs to reject bad arguments.

DOLIST.name: Do to list
DOLIST.description: Applies a program to corresponding elements of n lists of equal length and returns the list of results; the count may be omitted when the program takes one argument.

examples.comment: Two lists, the count 2, and a program that multiplies each pair

DOMAIN.description: Determines where an expression of the current variable is defined, returning a list of interval bounds marked as defined or undefined.

DOSUBS.name: Do to sublists
DOSUBS.description: Slides a window of n consecutive elements along a list and applies a program to each window, collecting the results in a new list. Inside the program NSUB and ENDSUB give the window position and count.

examples.comment: Adds each pair of neighbouring elements
SWAP - subtracts the earlier element from the later one in each pair

DOT.name: Dot product
DOT.description: Computes the scalar (dot) product of two real or complex vectors that have the same length.

DRAW.description: Plots the current equation EQ into the graphics picture using the plot type and parameters in PPAR, without drawing axes or erasing first.
DRAW.skip: draws into the graphics picture and returns nothing to the stack

28s.description: Plots the current equation EQ on the display, drawing the axes first and using the plot parameters in PPAR. An equation with two sides plots as two curves.

DRAW3DMATRIX.name: Draw 3D matrix
DRAW3DMATRIX.description: Draws a matrix as a 3D bar chart, one bar per element, with heights scaled between a given minimum and maximum value.
DRAW3DMATRIX.skip: draws into the graphics screen and returns nothing to the stack

DRAX.name: Draw axes
DRAX.description: Draws the axes defined in PPAR into the graphics picture.
DRAX.skip: draws into the graphics picture and returns nothing to the stack

28s.description: Draws the plot axes on the display, crossing at the point set in PPAR, with a tick mark every 10 pixels.

DROITE.name: Straight line
DROITE.description: Returns the equation of the straight line through two points of the plane, given as complex numbers or coordinate pairs.

DROP2.name: Drop two
DROP2.description: Discards the top two stack objects.

DROPN.name: Drop n objects
DROPN.description: Removes a given number of objects from the stack, not counting the count argument itself.

DRWΣ.name: Draw statistics plot
DRWΣ.description: Draws the axes and then a scatter plot of the points in ΣDAT, taking the two columns chosen in ΣPAR.
DRWΣ.skip: draws on the display and returns nothing to the stack

DTAG.name: Delete tag
DTAG.description: Removes every tag from a tagged object and leaves the bare object; untagged objects are returned unchanged.

DUP2.name: Duplicate two
DUP2.description: Duplicates the top two stack objects, keeping their order.
DUP2.stack: obj1 obj2 → obj1 obj2 obj1 obj2

DUPDUP.name: Duplicate twice
DUPDUP.description: Pushes two extra copies of the level 1 object.

DUPN.name: Duplicate n objects
DUPN.description: Duplicates the given number of top stack objects as a block, keeping their order.
DUPN.stack: obj1 … objn n → obj1 … objn obj1 … objn

examples.comment: The count 2 copies the top two objects, the 2 and the 3

D→R.name: Degrees to radians
D→R.description: Converts an angle in degrees to radians, independent of the current angle mode.

EDIT.description: Opens an object in the command-line editor and returns the edited version when the edit is confirmed.
EDIT.skip: opens an interactive editor and waits for the user

EDITB.name: Edit in best editor
EDITB.description: Opens an object in the editor best suited to its type, such as the matrix writer for arrays or the equation writer for algebraics, and returns the edited version.
EDITB.skip: opens an interactive editor and waits for the user

EGCD.name: Extended greatest common divisor
EGCD.description: Extended Euclid for polynomials: given a and b, returns their greatest common divisor c together with polynomials u and v satisfying a*u+b*v=c.

examples.comment: Returns c, u, v with (X^2+1)*u+(X-1)*v=c

EGV.name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
EGV.description: For a square matrix, returns its eigenvalues together with a matrix whose columns are the matching right eigenvectors.

EGVL.name: Eigenvalues
EGVL.description: For a square matrix, returns a vector holding its eigenvalues.

examples.comment: A quarter-turn rotation matrix has the eigenvalues i and -i

ELSE.description: Inside IF and IFERR structures, starts the clause that runs when the test is false or no error occurred.
ELSE.skip: fragment of IF ... THEN ... ELSE ... END; see IF for a complete example

END.description: Closes an IF, IFERR, CASE, WHILE or DO structure (and each THEN clause inside CASE).
END.skip: closes a program structure and cannot run alone; see IF, CASE, DO, WHILE

28s.description: Closes an IF, IFERR, WHILE or DO structure.

ENDSUB.name: Ending sublist
ENDSUB.description: Inside a DOSUBS program, returns the total number of windows that DOSUBS processes.

examples.comment: Windows of one element give 3 windows, so ENDSUB is 3 every time

ENG.name: Engineering mode
ENG.description: Sets engineering display: like scientific, but with exponents in steps of three; n gives the significant digits after the first.

EPSX0.name: Epsilon to zero
EPSX0.description: Cleans an expression by replacing every number whose magnitude is below the value of the variable EPS with zero.

examples.comment: 1E-15 is below EPS, so its term becomes 0

EQNLIB.name: Equation library
EQNLIB.description: Opens the Equation Library browser, where built-in sets of engineering and physics equations can be picked and solved.
EQNLIB.skip: opens an interactive catalog that waits for keys

EQW.name: Equation Writer
EQW.description: Edits an expression graphically in the Equation Writer and returns the edited result.
EQW.skip: opens the interactive equation writer and waits for the user

EQ→.name: Equation to stack
EQ→.description: Breaks an equation apart, leaving the left-hand side and the right-hand side as two separate objects; an expression without an equals sign comes back unchanged together with 0.

ER.name: Assembly errors
ER.description: After a failed ASM, shows the list of assembly errors and lets the user jump to each one in the source editor. Part of the development library.
ER.skip: opens an interactive error browser for the assembler

ERASE.description: Clears the graphics picture PICT to all blank pixels, keeping its size.
ERASE.skip: clears the graphics picture and returns nothing to the stack

ERR0.name: Clear last error
ERR0.description: Clears the record of the last error, so that ERRN afterwards gives #0 and ERRM an empty string.

examples.run: « IFERR 1. 0. / THEN END ERR0 ERRN » EVAL
examples.comment: Traps 1/0, clears the error record, then ERRN gives #0

ERRM.name: Error message
ERRM.description: Returns the message text of the most recent error as a string, or an empty string when there is none. Handy for reporting a trapped error from an IFERR structure.

28s.description: Returns the message of the most recent error as a string. Handy for reporting a trapped error from an IFERR structure.

ERRN.name: Error number
ERRN.description: Returns the code of the most recent error as a binary integer, or #0 when no error has occurred or the record was cleared. Mostly used in the THEN clause of an IFERR structure.

examples.comment: 305h, 773 in decimal, is the code of Infinite Result

28s.description: Returns the number of the most recent error as a binary integer. Mostly used in the THEN clause of an IFERR structure.

EULER.name: Euler's totient
EULER.description: Evaluates Euler's totient function: how many positive integers up to n are coprime to n.

examples.comment: 13 is prime, so 12 numbers up to it are coprime to it

EVAL.name: Evaluate
EVAL.description: Evaluates an object: a program runs, a name is replaced by what its variable holds, an algebraic is computed with the current variable values, and a list has its elements executed in turn. Data objects such as reals return themselves.

28s.description: Evaluates an object: a program runs, a name is replaced by what its variable holds, and an algebraic is computed with the current variable values. Data objects such as reals and lists return themselves.

EXGET.name: Get subexpression
EXGET.description: Returns the subexpression at position n of an algebraic: the object there together with its arguments. Positions count the objects from the left as written.

examples.comment: The 2nd object is +, so its subexpression is A+B

EXLR.name: Extract left and right sides
EXLR.description: Splits an equation into two objects: its left-hand side and its right-hand side.

EXP.name: Natural exponential
EXP.description: Natural exponential e^x, for reals, complex numbers and algebraics.

examples.comment: e^i has real part cos 1 and imaginary part sin 1, in radians

EXP&LN.name: Exponential and logarithm menu
EXP&LN.description: Opens the CAS menu of commands that rewrite exponentials and logarithms.

EXP2HYP.name: Exponential to hyperbolic
EXP2HYP.description: Rewrites exponentials in an expression in terms of hyperbolic sine and cosine.

EXP2POW.name: Exponential to power
EXP2POW.description: Rewrites exponentials of the form EXP(N*LN(X)) as the power X^N.

EXPAN.name: Expand products
EXPAN.description: Expands an expression one step by multiplying out products and powers over sums; repeat it to expand further.

EXPAND.description: Multiplies out products and integer powers in an algebraic expression and collects like terms.

EXPANDMOD.name: Expand modulo
EXPANDMOD.description: Expands a polynomial or integer expression and reduces its coefficients modulo the current CAS modulus.

examples.comment: Modulo 7 the X term vanishes and 12 becomes -2

EXPFIT.name: Exponential curve fit
EXPFIT.description: Selects the exponential model y = b·e^(m·x) for later regressions, stored in ΣPAR.

EXPLN.name: To exponentials and logarithms
EXPLN.description: Rewrites trigonometric and hyperbolic functions in an expression using only EXP and LN.

EXPM.name: Exponential minus 1
EXPM.description: Computes e^x - 1 without the loss of precision that subtracting 1 from EXP of a tiny x would cause.

examples.comment: The final 5 is the x²/2 term, a digit EXP(x)-1 would round away

EXSUB.name: Substitute subexpression
EXSUB.description: Replaces the subexpression at position n of an algebraic, the object there with its arguments, by another algebraic or name.

examples.comment: Replaces the + subexpression, A+B, with E^F

EYEPT.name: Eye point
EYEPT.description: Sets the eye position (x, y, z) of the viewer for perspective 3D plots, storing it in VPAR; the eye must sit in front of the view volume along y.

F0λ.name: Black body emissive power
F0λ.description: Returns the fraction of the total power radiated by a black body at temperature T that lies at wavelengths from zero up to λ. Takes the wavelength in metres and the temperature in kelvins, or unit objects.

examples.comment: Wavelength 500 nm (5E-7 m), temperature 5800 K
Wavelength 10 micrometres (0.00001 m), temperature 300 K

FACT.name: Factorial
FACT.description: Factorial of a non-negative integer, or the gamma function Γ(x+1) for other reals; an older spelling of the ! command kept for compatibility.

28s.description: Factorial of a non-negative integer, or the gamma function Γ(x+1) for other reals. Symbolic arguments give a symbolic result.

FACTOR.description: Splits a polynomial or rational expression into irreducible factors; given an integer, it returns its prime factorization.

FACTORMOD.name: Factor modulo
FACTORMOD.description: Factors a polynomial over the integers modulo the current CAS modulus, which has to be a small prime.

FACTORS.description: Breaks an integer or polynomial into its irreducible factors and returns a list alternating each factor with its multiplicity.

examples.comment: Each factor is followed by its multiplicity: 5, 3 squared, 2 cubed

FANNING.name: Fanning friction factor
FANNING.description: Computes the Fanning friction factor for flow in a pipe from the relative roughness and the Reynolds number, using the laminar formula at low Reynolds numbers and a turbulent correlation otherwise.

examples.comment: Relative roughness 0.0001, Reynolds number 100000
Zero roughness at Reynolds number 1000 gives 16 divided by 1000

FAST3D.name: Fast 3D plot type
FAST3D.description: Selects the fast 3D plot type, which draws a quickly rotatable wireframe of a function of two variables; the choice is kept in PPAR.

FC?.name: Flag clear?
FC?.description: Tests whether a flag is clear, returning 1 if it is clear and 0 if it is set. The flag is left unchanged.

FC?C.name: Flag clear? Then clear
FC?C.description: Reports whether a flag is clear (1) or set (0) and then clears it.

examples.comment: Flag 5 is set, so 0 comes back, and then flag 5 is cleared

FCOEF.name: Fraction from roots and poles
FCOEF.description: Builds the rational function whose roots and poles are given in a vector of value/multiplicity pairs, poles having negative multiplicity.

examples.comment: Root 1 twice (multiplicity 2) and a pole at 3 (multiplicity -1)
Root 0 once and root 2 once

FDISTRIB.name: Full distribute
FDISTRIB.description: Fully distributes multiplication over addition throughout an expression, in one go.

FFT.name: Fast Fourier transform
FFT.description: Applies the discrete Fourier transform to an array whose dimensions are powers of two, giving a complex array of the same size.

examples.comment: A single 1 followed by zeros gives a flat spectrum

FILER.name: File manager
FILER.description: Starts the file manager for browsing, copying, moving and deleting variables across directories and ports.
FILER.skip: opens the interactive file manager and waits for the user

FINDALARM.name: Find alarm
FINDALARM.description: Searches the alarm list and returns the index of the earliest alarm falling due after a given date or { date time } list, or of the first past-due alarm when given 0; returns 0 when none matches.
FINDALARM.stack: date → n; { date time } → n; 0 → n

examples.comment: The alarm, on 1 January 2030, falls due after 1 January 2029
The alarm is at 12:00, before 13:00, so none is found
0 looks for a past-due alarm, and none is due

FINISH.name: Finish server mode
FINISH.description: Tells a remote Kermit server to end server mode.
FINISH.skip: talks over the serial or IR port

FIX.name: Fixed mode
FIX.description: Sets fixed-point display with the given number of decimal places (0 to 11).

examples.comment: Zero decimal places rounds 12.7 up and keeps the point

FLASHEVAL.name: Evaluate flash function
FLASHEVAL.description: Evaluates a routine in flash ROM given its flash-pointer number as a binary integer; a low-level tool for programmers.
FLASHEVAL.skip: jumps into raw ROM code by address; a wrong value can crash the calculator

FLOOR.description: Rounds a real number down to the nearest integer not greater than it, so negative fractions move away from zero.

28s.description: Rounds a real number down to the nearest integer not greater than it, so negative fractions move away from zero.

FONT6.description: Puts the built-in 6-pixel-high system font on the stack as a font object, for example to make it the current font with →FONT.

FONT7.description: Returns the built-in 7-pixel-high system font as a font object.

FONT8.description: Returns the built-in 8-pixel-high system font as a font object.

FONT→.name: Current system font
FONT→.description: Returns the font object currently used as the system font.

FOR.description: Starts a counted loop with a named local counter that runs from a start value to an end value, closed by NEXT (step 1) or STEP (step taken from the stack).

examples.comment: Adds k from 1 to 5 to the 0 already on the stack
Counts from 1 to 10 in steps of 3

FORM.name: Form algebraic expression
FORM.description: Opens an interactive editor for rearranging an algebraic or equation by identities, so its value does not change. Leaving with the EXGET menu key also returns a chosen subexpression and its position.
FORM.skip: opens an interactive editor and waits for keys

FOURIER.name: Fourier coefficient
FOURIER.description: Computes the coefficient of index n of the complex Fourier series of an expression in the current variable; the period is read from the variable PERIOD and complex mode must be on.

FP.name: Fractional part
FP.description: Returns what follows the decimal point of a real: the number minus its integer part, so the result keeps the argument's sign.

28s.description: Returns what follows the decimal point of a real: the number minus its integer part, so the result keeps the argument's sign.

FREE.name: Free RAM card
FREE.description: Turns merged card RAM back into an independent port, moving the listed backup or library objects into it.

FREE1.name: Free port 1 RAM
FREE1.description: Detaches previously merged port 1 RAM from user memory so it becomes an independent port again, moving any named backup or library objects into it.
FREE1.skip: needs merged RAM in port 1 and changes the memory configuration

FREEZE.description: Keeps selected display areas (status area, stack area, menu labels, coded as a bit sum 1, 2, 4) from being redrawn when a program ends, so its screen output stays visible.
FREEZE.skip: only affects what the screen shows after a program ends

FROOTS.name: Fraction roots and poles
FROOTS.description: Finds the roots and poles of a rational function and returns them in a vector of value/multiplicity pairs, poles with negative multiplicity.

FS?.name: Flag set?
FS?.description: Tests whether a flag is set, returning 1 if it is and 0 if it is clear. The flag itself is left unchanged.

FS?C.name: Flag set? Then clear
FS?C.description: Reports whether a flag is set (1) or clear (0) and then clears it, which suits one-shot signalling between program parts.

examples.comment: Returns 1 because flag 5 is set, then clears it, so FS? gives 0

FUNCTAB.name: Function table
FUNCTAB.description: Opens the table view of a function plot, listing x values with the corresponding function values.

FUNCTION.name: Function plot type
FUNCTION.description: Selects the function plot type, which draws EQ as y versus the independent variable.

FXND.name: Fraction to numerator and denominator
FXND.description: Splits a fraction, or an expression that simplifies to one, into its numerator and denominator.

GAMMA.description: Evaluates the gamma function, which extends the factorial to real and complex arguments (Γ(n) equals (n-1)! for positive integers).

GAUSS.description: Diagonalises a quadratic form by Gauss's method, returning the diagonal coefficients, the change-of-basis matrix, the form rewritten as a sum of squares, and the variables.

GBASIS.name: Groebner basis
GBASIS.description: Computes a Groebner basis of the ideal generated by a vector of polynomials, using the listed variables in the given order.

GCD.name: Greatest common divisor
GCD.description: Computes the greatest common divisor for two integers or for two polynomials.

GCDMOD.name: Greatest common divisor modulo
GCDMOD.description: Computes the polynomial greatest common divisor for two polynomials whose coefficients are reduced modulo the current CAS modulus.

GET.description: Fetches the element at a given position of an array or list (a {row col} list for matrices); a variable name may stand for the object.
GET.stack: [array] n → x; {list} n → obj; 'name' n → obj

examples.comment: Row 2, column 1 of the matrix

GETI.name: Get and increment index
GETI.description: Like GET, but keeps the array or list and the advanced position on the stack under the fetched element, ready for stepping through all elements; the index wraps at the end and flag -64 is set.
GETI.stack: [array] n → [array] n+1 x; {list} n → {list} n+1 obj

examples.comment: The list, the next position 2, and the element at position 1
After position 3 the index wraps round to 1

28s.description: Like GET, but leaves the array or list, then the position after the one fetched, on the stack below the element, ready for stepping through all elements. After the last element the position wraps to 1 and flag 46 is set.
28s.stack: [array] n → [array] n+1 x; {list} n → {list} n+1 obj; 'name' n → 'name' n+1 obj

GOR.name: Graphics OR
GOR.description: Overlays one graphics object onto another at a given position by OR-ing their pixels; when the target is PICT the graphics picture is changed in place.
GOR.stack: grob1 (x,y) grob2 → grob1'; grob1 {#x #y} grob2 → grob1'; PICT pos grob2 →

examples.comment: ORs a 4 by 4 graphic into an 8 by 8 one at pixel 0, 0; the size is unchanged

GRAD.name: Grads mode
GRAD.description: Selects grads (400 to a full circle) as the angle unit for trigonometric functions and polar displays.

examples.comment: 100 grads is a quarter circle, so its sine is 1

GRAMSCHMIDT.description: Turns a set of vectors into an orthonormal basis of the same space, using a scalar product given as a program of two arguments.

GRAPH.description: Shows the graphics picture PICT and enters the interactive graphics environment with cursor movement and the graphics menu.
GRAPH.skip: opens the interactive graphics screen and waits for keys

GREDUCE.name: Groebner reduce
GREDUCE.description: Reduces a polynomial modulo a Groebner basis, returning the remainder of the division by the basis polynomials.

GRIDMAP.name: Grid map plot type
GRIDMAP.description: Selects the grid-mapping plot as the current plot type, which shows how a complex-valued function of a complex variable deforms a rectangular grid.

GROB.name: Graphics object
GROB.description: Introduces a graphics object in source text, followed by its width, height and pixel data in hexadecimal.

examples.comment: 8 pixels wide and 2 high: FF is the first row, 00 the second

GROBADD.name: Add graphics objects
GROBADD.description: Joins two graphics objects into one, placing the second below the first.

GXOR.name: Graphics exclusive OR
GXOR.description: Combines one graphics object into another at a given position by XOR-ing their pixels, so repeating it restores the original; PICT can be the target.
GXOR.stack: grob1 (x,y) grob2 → grob1'; grob1 {#x #y} grob2 → grob1'; PICT pos grob2 →

HADAMARD.name: Hadamard product
HADAMARD.description: Multiplies two matrices of the same dimensions element by element (the Hadamard product).

HALFTAN.name: Half-angle tangent
HALFTAN.description: Rewrites sines, cosines and tangents in an expression in terms of the tangent of the half angle.

HALT.description: Suspends the running program and returns to the keyboard with the program still pending; CONT resumes it and SST steps through it.
HALT.skip: suspends the program and waits for the user to continue

HEAD.description: Returns the leading item of a list, or the leading character of a string.

HEADER→.name: Header size
HEADER→.description: Returns how many lines the status header currently occupies above the stack.

HELP.description: Opens the built-in CAS help browser, listing the CAS commands with a short explanation and example for each.

HERMITE.name: Hermite polynomial
HERMITE.description: Builds the Hermite polynomial of degree n in the current CAS variable, as an exact symbolic expression.

HESS.name: Hessian
HESS.description: Computes the Hessian matrix of an expression for a vector of variables, also returning the gradient and the variables.

HEX.name: Hexadecimal mode
HEX.description: Selects base 16 for displaying binary integers.

examples.comment: 255 decimal is FF in hexadecimal
Binary 11111111 is FF in hexadecimal

HILBERT.name: Hilbert matrix
HILBERT.description: Builds the n×n Hilbert matrix, whose entry in row i, column j is 1/(i+j-1).

HISTOGRAM.name: Histogram plot type
HISTOGRAM.description: Selects the histogram plot type, which counts the values of one ΣDAT column into bins and draws the frequencies as bars.

HISTPLOT.name: Draw histogram plot
HISTPLOT.description: Draws a frequency histogram of a column of ΣDAT into the graphics picture.
HISTPLOT.skip: draws into the graphics picture and returns nothing to the stack

HMS+.name: Hours-minutes-seconds plus
HMS+.description: Adds two values given in HH.MMSS form and returns the sum in the same form.

examples.comment: 1h30m plus 2h45m gives 4h15m
0h59m59s plus 1 second carries over to exactly 1 hour

48sx.note: The 48SX's ROM gets some sums that carry into the next hour wrong: 0.5959 0.0001 HMS+ gives .6 instead of 1 (the 48GX gives 1). HMS→, + and →HMS give the right result.

HMS-.name: Hours-minutes-seconds minus
HMS-.description: Subtracts the HH.MMSS value in level 1 from the one in level 2 and returns the difference in HH.MMSS form.

examples.comment: 4h15m minus 1h30m gives 2h45m
1 hour minus 1 second gives 0h59m59s

HMS→.name: Hours-minutes-seconds to decimal
HMS→.description: Converts a value in HH.MMSS form to decimal hours (or degrees).

examples.comment: 1h30m is 1.5 hours
2h45m09s is 2.7525 hours

HOME.description: Makes HOME, the top of the directory tree, the current directory, wherever you are in a subdirectory.

HORNER.name: Horner's scheme
HORNER.description: Applies Horner's scheme to divide a polynomial by (X-a), returning the quotient, the point a, and the value of the polynomial at a.

examples.comment: Divides by (X-3): the quotient, the point 3, and the value at 3
Divides by (X+1): the quotient, the point -1, and the value at -1

HYPERBOLIC.description: Opens the CAS menu or selection list of hyperbolic functions and their inverses.
HYPERBOLIC.skip: opens a menu or a selection screen

H→.name: Hex to object
H→.description: Rebuilds an object from a string of hexadecimal digits giving its nibbles, the inverse of →H; needs library 256 attached.

H→A.name: Hex to address
H→A.description: Converts a five-digit hexadecimal string in nibble order to the address it encodes, as a binary integer; the inverse of A→H. Needs library 256 attached.

H→S.name: Hex to string
H→S.description: Converts a string of hexadecimal digits in nibble order back into the characters they encode, the inverse of S→H; needs library 256 attached.

examples.comment: Each character is two digits in reverse order: 41 is A, 42 is B

IABCUV.name: Integer Bézout equation
IABCUV.description: Finds integers u and v solving a*u+b*v=c for given integers a, b and c; c must be a multiple of the gcd of a and b.

examples.comment: Finds u and v with 6*u + 11*v = 3
Finds u and v with 4*u + 6*v = 10

IBASIS.name: Intersection basis
IBASIS.description: Returns a basis of the intersection of the two subspaces spanned by two lists of vectors.

IBP.name: Integration by parts
IBP.description: Performs one step of integration by parts: given an integrand written as u*v' and the antiderivative v, it returns u*v and the remaining integrand -u'*v.

ICHINREM.name: Integer Chinese remainder
ICHINREM.description: Solves two simultaneous integer congruences, each given as a vector [value modulus], with the Chinese remainder theorem.

examples.comment: x is 2 modulo 3 and 1 modulo 5, giving -4 modulo 15

IDIV2.name: Integer division
IDIV2.description: Divides one integer by another and returns the integer quotient and the remainder.

IDN.name: Identity matrix
IDN.description: Builds an n×n identity matrix, or replaces a square matrix (or one stored under a name) with the identity matrix of the same size.

IEGCD.name: Integer extended greatest common divisor
IEGCD.description: Extended Euclid for integers: given a and b, returns their greatest common divisor c and Bezout coefficients u and v with a*u+b*v=c.

examples.comment: 6*2 + 11*-1 = 1, so the gcd is 1

IF.description: Opens a conditional structure, IF test THEN commands [ELSE other commands] END: the test runs, and the nonzero or zero value it leaves decides which commands execute. Only valid inside programs.

examples.run: « IF DUP 3. > THEN "big" ELSE "small" END » EVAL
« IF DUP 3. > THEN "big" ELSE "small" END » EVAL

IFERR.name: If error
IFERR.description: Opens an error trap, IFERR commands THEN on-error [ELSE on-success] END: if any command after IFERR fails, the program goes on with the THEN part instead of stopping. ERRN and ERRM tell which error occurred.

examples.comment: 1/0 fails, so the THEN part runs and pushes the text; the 1 and 0 stay

IFFT.name: Inverse fast Fourier transform
IFFT.description: Undoes FFT: applies the inverse discrete Fourier transform to an array whose dimensions are powers of two.

IFT.name: If-then
IFT.description: Evaluates an object only when a test value is nonzero; when the test is zero both arguments are dropped. The one-branch counterpart of IFTE.

examples.comment: The test 1 is not zero, so the program runs: 2 plus 3

IFTE.name: If-then-else
IFTE.description: Chooses between two objects by a test value: a nonzero test gives the first alternative, zero gives the second, and the chosen object is evaluated. With a symbolic test it returns an IFTE expression, which makes it usable as a conditional function inside algebraics.

ILAP.name: Inverse Laplace transform
ILAP.description: Computes the inverse Laplace transform of an expression in the current CAS variable.

IM.name: Imaginary part
IM.description: Extracts the imaginary component of a complex value, or of every element of a complex array; a real argument gives 0.

IMAGE.description: Returns a basis of the image (column space) of a linear map given by its matrix.

INCR.name: Increment
INCR.description: Adds 1 to a variable holding a real number, stores it, and returns the new value.

INDEP.name: Independent variable
INDEP.description: Sets the independent variable for plotting by writing a name into the reserved PPAR variable; a list form can also give its plotting range.

examples.comment: A list also sets the range of the variable: T from 0 to 5

28s.description: Sets the independent variable for plotting by storing a name as the third item of PPAR.

INFORM.name: Input form
INFORM.description: Shows a full-screen input form with labelled fields, then returns the entered values and a flag telling whether the user confirmed or cancelled. Takes a title, field specifications, a layout, reset values and initial values.
INFORM.skip: waits for the user to fill in an interactive input form

INPUT.description: Halts a program to show a prompt string and open the command line with given initial text, then returns what the user typed as a string once ENTER is pressed.
INPUT.skip: waits for the user to edit and confirm the command line

INT.name: Integrate
INT.description: Integrates an expression symbolically with respect to a variable and evaluates the antiderivative at a given point or expression; a CAS command.

examples.comment: Integrates X^2 in X, evaluated at Y

INTEGER.description: Opens the CAS menu or selection list of integer arithmetic commands (divisors, primes, GCD and related).
INTEGER.skip: opens a menu or a selection screen

INTVX.name: Integrate in the current variable
INTVX.description: Finds an antiderivative of an expression in the current CAS variable (VX, normally X).

INV.name: Inverse
INV.description: Computes the reciprocal 1/x of a real, complex or unit object; for a square matrix it returns the matrix inverse.

28s.description: Computes 1/x for a real or a complex number; for a square matrix it returns the matrix inverse.

INVMOD.name: Inverse modulo
INVMOD.description: Gives the multiplicative inverse of an integer modulo the current CAS modulus.

examples.comment: Modulo 7, so 2 times -3 gives 1
Modulo 11, so 3 times 4 gives 1

IP.name: Integer part
IP.description: Truncates a real number to its whole-number part by dropping the fractional digits, keeping the sign; units are kept.

28s.description: Truncates a real number to its whole-number part by dropping the fractional digits, keeping the sign.

IQUOT.name: Integer quotient
IQUOT.description: Returns the integer quotient when one integer is divided by another in the Euclidean sense, discarding the remainder.

IREMAINDER.name: Integer remainder
IREMAINDER.description: Returns the remainder left when one integer is divided by another.

ISOL.name: Isolate variable
ISOL.description: Rearranges an equation or expression to make the given variable stand alone, returning an equation for it; with general solutions it may introduce s1 and n1 placeholders.

28s.description: Rearranges an equation or expression so that the variable's first appearance stands alone, and returns what that variable equals, not an equation; general solutions may bring in the s1 and n1 placeholders.

ISOM.name: Isometry
ISOM.description: Analyses the matrix of a linear isometry in 2 or 3 dimensions and returns its characteristic elements, such as the rotation angle, with a sign telling a rotation from a reflection.

ISPRIME?.name: Is prime?
ISPRIME?.description: Tests whether an integer is prime, returning 1 for a prime and 0 otherwise.

examples.comment: 91 is 7 times 13, so it is not prime

I→R.name: Integer to real
I→R.description: Turns an exact integer into the equivalent real number; applied to a symbolic expression, it converts the integers inside it.

JORDAN.name: Jordan reduction
JORDAN.description: Analyses a square matrix: returns its minimal polynomial, characteristic polynomial, the eigenspaces (or Jordan chains) tagged by eigenvalue, and the eigenvalues with multiplicity.

KER.name: Kernel
KER.description: Returns a basis of the kernel (null space) of a linear map given by its matrix.

KERRM.name: Kermit error message
KERRM.description: Returns the text of the last Kermit error packet received, or an empty string.
KERRM.skip: reports the state of the serial or IR link

KEY.description: Checks the keyboard buffer without waiting: if a key has been pressed it returns the key's row-column code and 1, otherwise just 0. Used in polling loops that react to keys.

28s.description: Checks the key buffer without waiting: if a key is waiting it removes it and returns a string naming the key and 1, otherwise only 0. Used in polling loops that react to keys.

KEYEVAL.name: Evaluate key
KEYEVAL.description: Performs the action of the key given by its row-column-plane key code, as if that key had been pressed.
KEYEVAL.skip: simulates a keypress, whose effect depends on the interactive keyboard state

KEYTIME→.name: Key debounce time
KEYTIME→.description: Returns the current keyboard debounce time in clock ticks.

KGET.name: Kermit get
KGET.description: Asks a Kermit server for one or more files and stores each in a variable.
KGET.skip: talks over the serial or IR port

KILL.description: Ends the running program at once, together with any suspended (halted) programs, and returns control to the keyboard. Objects already on the stack stay there.
KILL.skip: aborts the running program, and with it the server command that runs the example

LABEL.name: Label axes
LABEL.description: Writes numeric labels at the ends of the axes in the graphics picture.
LABEL.skip: draws into the graphics picture and returns nothing to the stack

LAGRANGE.name: Lagrange interpolation
LAGRANGE.description: Finds the lowest-degree polynomial passing through a set of points given as a two-row matrix, the x values in the first row and the y values in the second (Lagrange interpolation).

examples.comment: The points (1,2), (2,5) and (3,10)
The points (0,1) and (1,3)

LANGUAGE→.name: Current language
LANGUAGE→.description: Returns the number of the language currently used for system messages (0 English, 1 French, 2 Spanish).

LAP.name: Laplace transform
LAP.description: Computes the Laplace transform of an expression in the current CAS variable; the result uses the same variable as the transform variable.

LAPL.name: Laplacian
LAPL.description: Computes the Laplacian (sum of the second partial derivatives) of an expression for a vector of variables.

LAST.name: Last arguments
LAST.description: Puts back copies of what the last command with arguments took from the stack, at the levels they came from. Works only while LAST mode (flag 31) is on.
LAST.stack: → obj; → obj1 obj2; → obj1 obj2 obj3

LASTARG.name: Last arguments
LASTARG.description: Puts back on the stack the arguments consumed by the most recent command that took any, which is handy after an operation used the wrong values. Works only while last-argument saving (flag -55 clear) is on.

examples.comment: The one argument, 16, comes back after the square root

LCD→.name: Display to graphics object
LCD→.description: Copies the current screen contents into a 131 by 64 pixel graphics object on the stack.

28s.name: Display to string
28s.description: Returns the current display as a 548-character string, one character for each column of eight pixels; →LCD shows such a string again.

LCM.name: Least common multiple
LCM.description: Computes the least common multiple of a pair of integers or a pair of polynomials.

LCXM.name: Matrix from program
LCXM.description: Builds a matrix of a given number of rows and columns by running a two-argument program on each row index i and column index j to produce that entry.

examples.comment: Entry (i,j) is i plus j, for 2 rows and 3 columns
A 3 by 3 multiplication table

LC~C.name: Long complex conversion
LC~C.description: Converts a complex number into the internal extended-precision (long) complex form, or a long complex back into an ordinary complex. Part of the development library.

LDEC.name: Linear differential equation
LDEC.description: Solves a constant-coefficient linear ODE given its right-hand side and characteristic polynomial, or a first-order linear system given a vector of constant terms and a coefficient matrix.

examples.comment: The right-hand side is 0 and the characteristic polynomial is X^2+1

LEGENDRE.name: Legendre polynomial
LEGENDRE.description: Builds the Legendre polynomial of degree n in the current CAS variable, as an exact symbolic expression.

LGCD.name: List greatest common divisor
LGCD.description: Computes the greatest common divisor of all elements of a list of integers or expressions, leaving the list in place below the result.

LIBEVAL.name: Evaluate library function
LIBEVAL.description: Executes an unnamed library function selected by a binary integer that encodes library number and function number; a bad value can corrupt memory.
LIBEVAL.skip: calls arbitrary ROM or library code by address; wrong values can corrupt memory

LIBS.name: Libraries
LIBS.description: Lists each library attached in the directory you are in, giving its title, library number and port.

LIN.name: Linearize exponentials
LIN.description: Linearizes exponentials in an expression, merging products and powers of EXP terms into a single exponential of a sum.

LINE.description: Draws a straight line between two points of the graphics picture, given in user units or pixels.
LINE.skip: draws into the graphics picture and returns nothing to the stack

LINFIT.name: Linear curve fit
LINFIT.description: Selects the straight-line model y = b + m·x for later regressions, stored in ΣPAR.

LININ.name: Linear test
LININ.description: Tests whether an algebraic is linear in a given variable, meaning terms containing it are only added or subtracted and each is at most scaled by a factor free of it; returns 1 or 0.

examples.comment: SIN(Y) does not contain X, so the term is linear

LINSOLVE.name: Linear solve
LINSOLVE.description: Solves a linear system symbolically for the listed variables, returning the reduced system, the pivots and the solution.

LIST→.name: List to stack
LIST→.description: Takes a list apart, pushing each element onto the stack followed by the element count. Superseded by OBJ→ but still accepted.

28s.description: Takes a list apart, pushing each element onto the stack followed by the element count.

LN.name: Natural logarithm
LN.description: Natural logarithm. Negative reals give a complex result and zero is an infinite-result error unless flagged otherwise.
LN.stack: x → ln x; z → ln z; 'symb' → 'LN(symb)'

LNAME.name: List of names
LNAME.description: Collects the variable names that occur in a symbolic expression into a vector, keeping the expression on the stack.

LNCOLLECT.name: Collect logarithms
LNCOLLECT.description: Gathers sums and multiples of logarithms in an expression into the logarithm of a single product or power.

LNP1.name: Natural logarithm of 1+x
LNP1.description: Computes ln(1+x) accurately even when x is tiny, where adding 1 first would throw away digits; the argument must be greater than -1.

LOCAL.description: Creates local variables from a list of names or name=value equations, mainly for use inside algebraic programs.

LOG.name: Common logarithm (base 10)
LOG.description: Base-10 (common) logarithm of a real, a complex number or an algebraic; negative reals give a complex result.
LOG.stack: x → log x; z → log z; 'symb' → 'LOG(symb)'

LOGFIT.name: Logarithmic curve fit
LOGFIT.description: Selects the logarithmic model y = b + m·ln x for later regressions, stored in ΣPAR.

LQ.name: LQ factorization
LQ.description: Factors a rectangular matrix with row pivoting into a lower-trapezoidal L, an orthogonal Q and a permutation P, so that P·A = L·Q.

LR.name: Linear regression
LR.description: Fits a straight line by least squares to the two ΣDAT columns that XCOL and YCOL choose, returns its intercept and slope, and saves them in ΣPAR for PREDX, PREDY and ΣLINE.

28s.description: Fits a straight line to two columns of ΣDAT (chosen with COLΣ, by default 1 and 2) by least squares, returns its intercept and slope, and stores them in ΣPAR for PREDV.

LR~R.name: Long real conversion
LR~R.description: Converts a real number to an extended-precision long real, or a long real back to an ordinary real; needs library 256 attached.

LSQ.name: Least squares
LSQ.description: Solves A·X=B in the least-squares sense with minimum norm, for over-, under- or exactly determined systems; B is a vector or a matrix of right-hand sides.
