examples.comment: The vector is B, the matrix is A: three equations, two unknowns

LU.name: LU decomposition
LU.description: Factors a square matrix with partial pivoting into a lower-triangular L, an upper-triangular U with unit diagonal, and a permutation P, so that P·A = L·U.

LVAR.name: List of variables
LVAR.description: Lists the variables an algebraic object depends on, keeping the object itself on the stack.

examples.comment: SIN(X) is listed as a whole, not as X

MAD.name: Determinant, inverse and adjoint
MAD.description: Gives a square matrix's determinant, formal inverse, the matrix coefficients of the adjoint polynomial, and the characteristic polynomial.

MAIN.name: CAS main menu
MAIN.description: Opens the computer algebra system's main menu, which leads to its sub-menus.

MAKESTR.name: Make string
MAKESTR.description: Creates a string of the given length filled with filler characters, handy for testing or reserving memory. Part of the development library.

MANT.name: Mantissa
MANT.description: Returns the mantissa of a real number: its significant digits scaled into the range 1 to below 10, as in scientific notation.

MAP.description: Applies a program to each item of a list (or of an array) and collects the results in an object of the same shape.

MATHS.name: Mathematics menu
MATHS.description: Menu-entry word of the CAS that brings up the top-level menu of mathematics commands.

MATR.name: Matrix menu
MATR.description: Opens the CAS menu of matrix and linear algebra commands.

MAX.description: Takes two reals and keeps the larger of them; symbolic arguments give a symbolic MAX expression.

MAXR.name: Maximum real
MAXR.description: Puts the symbolic constant MAXR, the largest positive real the calculator can hold (9.99999999999E499), on the stack; it evaluates to a number when numeric results are requested or with →NUM.

MAXΣ.name: Statistics maximum
MAXΣ.description: Returns the largest value of each column of ΣDAT, as a real for single-column data or a vector otherwise.

MCALC.name: Make calculated value
MCALC.description: Marks one or more variables of the multiple-equation solver as calculated (unknowns to solve for), or all of them with "ALL".

MEAN.description: Returns the arithmetic mean of each column of ΣDAT, as a real for single-column data or a vector otherwise.

MEM.name: Memory available
MEM.description: Reports how many bytes of user memory are still free.

MENU.description: Displays a menu: a number selects a built-in menu (its code from the menu table, a decimal part picking the page), a list defines a custom menu which is also stored as the CST variable.
MENU.skip: changes the soft-key menu on the screen and returns nothing to the stack

28s.description: Shows a menu: a number from 1 to 24 selects a built-in menu, a list of commands and names makes a custom menu, and a list that starts with STO makes a menu whose keys store values into the named variables.

MENUXY.name: CAS command menu by number
MENUXY.description: Shows a soft-key menu holding the CAS commands whose numbers lie between the two given indices.
MENUXY.skip: only builds a soft-key menu on the screen

MERGE.name: Merge RAM card
MERGE.description: Joins the RAM of a plug-in card in the given port to main user memory, so its space is no longer an independent port.
MERGE.skip: needs a RAM card plugged into port 1 or 2

MERGE1.name: Merge port 1 RAM
MERGE1.description: Joins the RAM on a card in port 1 to main user memory, enlarging the space available for variables and the stack.
MERGE1.skip: needs a RAM card in port 1 and changes the memory configuration

MIN.description: Takes two reals and keeps the smaller of them; symbolic arguments give a symbolic MIN expression.

MINEHUNT.description: Starts the built-in Minehunt game, in which the player steers across a minefield guided by counts of nearby mines.
MINEHUNT.skip: interactive game that waits for keys

MINIFONT→.name: Current minifont
MINIFONT→.description: Returns the font object currently used as the minifont, so it can be saved, inspected or replaced.

MINIT.name: Multiple-equation solver initialization
MINIT.description: Prepares the multiple-equation solver by building the reserved variable Mpar from the equation list held in EQ.

MINR.name: Minimum real
MINR.description: Puts the symbolic constant MINR, the smallest positive real the calculator can hold (1.E-499), on the stack; →NUM or numeric-results mode turns it into the number.

MINΣ.name: Statistics minimum
MINΣ.description: Returns the smallest value of each column of ΣDAT, as a real for single-column data or a vector otherwise.

MITM.name: Multiple-equation menu item order
MITM.description: Sets the title and the menu variable order that the multiple-equation solver shows, updating Mpar.

MKISOM.name: Make isometry
MKISOM.description: Builds the matrix of a 2D or 3D linear isometry from its characteristic elements and a sign: 1 for a direct isometry (rotation), -1 for an indirect one.

examples.comment: A rotation by π/2; the sign 1 marks a direct isometry

MOD.name: Modulo
MOD.description: Computes the remainder of x divided by y using floored division, so the result has the sign of y (x - y·FLOOR(x/y)).
MOD.stack: x y → x mod y; 'symb' y → 'symb MOD y'

examples.comment: The result takes the sign of the divisor, so -17 mod 5 is 3

MODSTO.name: Store modulus
MODSTO.description: Sets the modulus used by the CAS modular-arithmetic commands; it is shown as the modulo field of the CAS settings.

examples.comment: Modulo 7, so 2 times -3 gives 1

MODULAR.description: Opens the CAS menu or selection list of modular arithmetic commands.
MODULAR.skip: opens a menu or a selection screen

MOLWT.name: Molecular weight
MOLWT.description: Computes the molecular weight of a chemical formula given as a string, using the element data of the periodic table library.

MROOT.name: Multiple-equation root
MROOT.description: Runs the multiple-equation solver to find the named variable from the known ones, chaining through the equations in Mpar as needed; "ALL" solves every variable it can.
MROOT.skip: needs an equation set prepared with MINIT and the multiple-equation solver

MSGBOX.name: Message box
MSGBOX.description: Shows a string in a framed message box and waits until the user dismisses it.
MSGBOX.skip: displays a message box and waits for a key

MSLV.name: Solve nonlinear system
MSLV.description: Solves a system of nonlinear equations numerically by Newton's method, from a vector of equations, a vector of unknowns and a vector of initial guesses.

MSOLVR.name: Multiple-equation solver
MSOLVR.description: Shows the Multiple-Equation Solver's variables menu for the equation set that Mpar describes, ready for entering knowns and solving unknowns.
MSOLVR.skip: installs an interactive solver menu; needs a prepared Mpar

MSOLVR2.description: Internal entry of the multiple-equation solver; not meant for direct use.
MSOLVR2.skip: internal solver entry that drives the solver menu screen

MULTMOD.name: Multiply modulo
MULTMOD.description: Multiplies two expressions or integers and reduces the product modulo the current CAS modulus.

MUSER.name: Make user-defined variable
MUSER.description: Marks one or more variables of the multiple-equation solver as user-defined (known inputs), or all of them with "ALL".

NDIST.name: Normal distribution
NDIST.description: Evaluates the normal (Gaussian) probability density with mean m and variance v at the point x.

NDUPN.name: Duplicate n times, keep count
NDUPN.description: Replaces an object and a count n with n copies of the object, followed by n itself.

NEG.name: Negate
NEG.description: Changes the sign of its argument: reals, complex numbers, arrays, unit objects and algebraics are negated element by element or symbolically.

28s.description: Changes the sign of its argument: reals, complex numbers, arrays and algebraics are negated element by element or symbolically.

NEWOB.name: New object
NEWOB.description: Makes a fresh, independent copy of an object in memory, releasing any hidden reference to a larger object it was taken from.

NEXT.description: Closes a START or FOR loop, adding 1 to the counter and repeating the body while the counter has not passed the final value.
NEXT.skip: closes a START or FOR loop and cannot run alone; see START for an example

NEXTPRIME.description: Returns the smallest prime number greater than the given integer.

NIP.name: Drop level 2
NIP.description: Removes the object on level 2, leaving the level 1 object in its place.

NOT.description: Inverts every bit of a binary integer within the current word size; for a real it is a logical negation, giving 1 for zero and 0 for anything else.

examples.comment: Every one of the 64 bits is inverted
The word size is 8, so only 8 bits are inverted

NOVAL.name: No value
NOVAL.description: Pushes the placeholder object that marks an empty field in INFORM reset and initial value lists, and that INFORM returns for fields left blank.

NSUB.name: Sublist number
NSUB.description: Inside a DOSUBS program, returns the position of the window currently being processed, counting from 1.

examples.comment: NSUB is 1, 2, 3 in turn, so each element is multiplied by its position

NUM.name: Character number
NUM.description: Returns the character code (0 to 255) of a string's leading character.

NUMX.name: Number of x-steps
NUMX.description: Sets how many sample points a 3D perspective plot takes along x for each y step, storing the count in VPAR.

NUMY.name: Number of y-steps
NUMY.description: Sets how many y steps a 3D perspective plot takes across the view volume, storing the count in VPAR.

NΣ.name: Number of data points
NΣ.description: Returns how many data points (rows) ΣDAT holds.

OBGET.name: Object get
OBGET.description: Returns the object at position n of an algebraic, inside a one-element list. Objects (names, numbers and functions) are counted from the left as the algebraic is written.

examples.comment: Counting A, +, B, * and C from the left, the 2nd is +
Counting A, * and B from the left, the 3rd is B

OBJ→.name: Object to stack
OBJ→.description: Takes a composite object apart: a list or program yields its elements and a count, a complex number its two parts, an array its elements and a dimension list, a tagged object its contents and tag, an algebraic its arguments, count and operator. A string is parsed and evaluated as command-line text.
OBJ→.stack: {list} → obj1 … objn n; (x,y) → x y; [array] → x1 … xn {dims}; :tag:obj → obj "tag"; "str" → result

OBSUB.name: Object substitute
OBSUB.description: Replaces the object at position n of an algebraic with the object in a one-element list, which may be a name, a number or a function. Positions are counted as for OBGET.

examples.comment: Replaces the 3rd object, B, with C
Replaces the 2nd object, the *, with +

OCT.name: Octal mode
OCT.description: Selects base 8 for displaying binary integers.

examples.comment: Decimal 64 is 100 in octal
Hexadecimal FF is 377 in octal

OFF.description: Switches the calculator off; when it is used inside a program, execution continues after the next power-on.

OLDPRT.name: Old printer
OLDPRT.description: Makes later printing remap characters for the older HP 82240A infrared printer by storing a remapping string in the PRTPAR variable.

OPENIO.name: Open I/O port
OPENIO.description: Opens the serial or infrared port with the settings in IOPAR, so it can receive Kermit commands or raw data.
OPENIO.skip: talks over the serial or IR port

OR.description: Bitwise OR of two binary integers; for reals it is a logical OR returning 1 when either value is non-zero, else 0. Symbolic arguments give a symbolic expression.

examples.comment: Binary 1100 OR 1010 gives 1110

ORDER.description: Moves the listed variables to the front of the directory you are in, in the order given, which also orders the VAR menu.

28s.description: Moves the listed variables to the front of the directory you are in, in the order given, which also orders the USER menu.

OVER.description: Duplicates the second stack object onto the top of the stack.

P2C.name: Permutation to cycles
P2C.description: Decomposes a permutation given as a list of images into disjoint cycles and returns them with the permutation's signature.

examples.comment: 1 goes to 3 and back, 2 goes to 4 and back
1 goes to 2, 2 to 3, and 3 back to 1

PA2B2.name: Prime as a²+b²
PA2B2.description: For a prime p equal to 2 or congruent to 1 modulo 4, finds a Gaussian integer a+bi with a^2+b^2=p; useful for factoring Gaussian integers.

examples.comment: 13 is 3 squared plus 2 squared
29 is 5 squared plus 2 squared

PARAMETRIC.name: Parametric plot type
PARAMETRIC.description: Selects the parametric plot type, where EQ yields a complex number whose real and imaginary parts give x and y for each parameter value.

PARAMTAB.name: Parametric table
PARAMTAB.description: Opens the table view of a parametric plot, listing parameter values with the corresponding x and y.

PARITY.description: Sets the serial parity stored in IOPAR as a code from 0 to 4 (none, odd, even, mark, space); a negative code disables parity checking of incoming data.
PARITY.skip: changes the parity of the serial link the examples run over

PARSURFACE.name: Parametric surface plot type
PARSURFACE.description: Selects the parametric surface plot as the current plot type, where EQ gives x, y and z as functions of two parameters ranging over the XXRNG and YYRNG plane.

PARTFRAC.name: Partial fractions
PARTFRAC.description: Decomposes a rational expression into a polynomial part plus a sum of partial fractions.

PATH.description: Returns the list of directory names from HOME down to the current directory.

PCAR.name: Characteristic polynomial
PCAR.description: Computes a square matrix's characteristic polynomial, written in the current CAS variable.

PCOEF.name: Polynomial from roots
PCOEF.description: Builds the monic polynomial that has the given roots and returns its coefficients as a vector, highest power first. The inverse of PROOT.

examples.comment: The roots 1 and 2 give X^2 - 3X + 2

PCONTOUR.name: Pseudo-contour plot type
PCONTOUR.description: Selects the pseudo-contour plot as the current plot type, which draws the level curves of a function z(x,y) seen from above.

PCOV.name: Population covariance
PCOV.description: Returns the population covariance between the two ΣDAT columns selected by XCOL and YCOL.

PDIM.name: Picture dimensions
PDIM.description: Changes the graphics picture: two complex numbers set the user-unit corners of the plot range in PPAR, two binary integers set the size of PICT in pixels.

examples.comment: (-5,-2) and (5,2) become the new minimum and maximum of the plot range

PEEK.description: Reads a given number of nibbles from memory starting at an address and returns them as a hexadecimal string; needs library 256 attached.

PEEKARM.name: Peek ARM memory
PEEKARM.description: Reads data directly from memory of the ARM processor on ARM-based models. Part of the development library.

PERINFO.name: Periodic table information
PERINFO.description: Shows information about the periodic table library.

PERM.name: Permutations
PERM.description: Gives the number of ordered arrangements of m items chosen from n: n!/(n-m)!.

PERTBL.name: Periodic table
PERTBL.description: Opens the periodic table application, an interactive table of the chemical elements.

PEVAL.name: Polynomial evaluation
PEVAL.description: Evaluates a polynomial, given as a coefficient vector with the highest power first, at a number.

examples.comment: X^2 - 3X + 2 evaluated at X=5
2X^3 + 1 evaluated at X=-1

PGDIR.name: Purge directory
PGDIR.description: Purges a directory with all variables and subdirectories it contains.

PICK.description: Pushes a copy of the object found at the given stack level (counted after removing the level argument).
PICK.stack: objn … obj1 n → objn … obj1 objn

examples.comment: Copies level 3, the 10, to level 1

PICK3.name: Pick level 3
PICK3.description: Pushes a copy of the object found on level 3.
PICK3.stack: x y z → x y z x

PICT.name: Picture
PICT.description: Pushes the name PICT, which stands for the graphics picture so that STO, RCL, GOR and similar commands can address it.

PICTURE.description: Switches the display to the graphics environment, showing the current PICT so it can be scrolled, annotated or edited with the cursor and drawing menu.
PICTURE.skip: enters the interactive graphics environment and waits for keys

PINIT.name: Port initialize
PINIT.description: Initializes all active memory-card ports, for example after inserting a card with several ports, without disturbing data already stored in them.
PINIT.skip: only reinitializes the plug-in card ports; nothing to show on the stack

PIX?.name: Pixel on?
PIX?.description: Tests one pixel of the graphics picture, given in user units or pixels, and returns 1 when it is on and 0 when it is off.

examples.comment: A pixel given as an {x y} list in pixels

PIXEL.description: Turns on the display pixel at the plot coordinates given as a complex number and sets the message flag, so the normal stack display does not replace it.
PIXEL.skip: draws into the display and returns nothing to the stack

PIXOFF.name: Pixel off
PIXOFF.description: Turns off the pixel of the graphics picture at the given coordinate, in user units or pixels.
PIXOFF.skip: draws into the graphics picture and returns nothing to the stack

PIXON.name: Pixel on
PIXON.description: Turns on the pixel of the graphics picture at the given coordinate, in user units or pixels.
PIXON.skip: draws into the graphics picture and returns nothing to the stack

PKT.name: Kermit packet
PKT.description: Sends a Kermit command packet of the given type and data to a server and returns its reply.
PKT.skip: talks over the serial or IR port

PLOT.description: Stores an expression as the current plot equation and opens the plot setup for it.

PLOTADD.name: Add to plot
PLOTADD.description: Appends an expression to the plot functions kept in the EQ variable.
PLOTADD.skip: does not return within the time limit when run headless on the 49G

PMAX.name: Picture maximum
PMAX.description: Sets the plot window's top-right corner in PPAR to the given coordinates, creating PPAR if needed.

PMIN.name: Picture minimum
PMIN.description: Sets the lower-left plot window corner in PPAR to the given coordinates, creating PPAR if needed.

PMINI.name: Minimal polynomial
PMINI.description: Computes the minimal polynomial of a square matrix, given as a matrix from whose last nonzero row the polynomial's coefficients are read.

POKE.description: Writes a string of hexadecimal digits into memory at the given address; needs library 256 attached and can corrupt memory.

POKEARM.name: Poke ARM memory
POKEARM.description: Writes data directly into memory of the ARM processor on ARM-based models. Part of the development library.

POLAR.name: Polar plot type
POLAR.description: Selects the polar plot type, which draws EQ as a radius depending on an angle.

POLARTAB.name: Polar table
POLARTAB.description: Opens the table view of a polar plot, listing angle values with the corresponding radius.

POLYNOMIAL.description: Opens the CAS menu or selection list of polynomial commands.
POLYNOMIAL.skip: opens a menu or a selection screen

POP.description: Restores the flag settings and current directory most recently saved by PUSH.

POS.name: Position
POS.description: Searches a string for a substring, or a list for an object, and returns where the first match starts; 0 means not found.

examples.comment: The first L is the 3rd character
The 7 is the 3rd element

POTENTIAL.description: Finds a scalar function whose gradient equals the given vector field, taken with respect to the listed variables; fails when the field is not a gradient.

examples.comment: The field (X,Y) in the variables X and Y
The field (Y,X) in the variables X and Y

POWEXPAND.name: Power expand
POWEXPAND.description: Rewrites an integer power as an explicit product of repeated factors, e.g. a cube as three equal factors.

POWMOD.name: Power modulo
POWMOD.description: Raises an expression or integer to an integer power, reducing modulo the current CAS modulus.

examples.comment: 3^5 is 243, and 243 is -2 modulo 7
(X+1)^3 modulo 3 loses the middle terms

PR1.name: Print level 1
PR1.description: Sends the top stack object to the printer and leaves it on the stack.
PR1.skip: prints to the infrared or serial printer

PREDV.name: Predicted value
PREDV.description: Predicts the dependent value for a given independent value using the regression model and coefficients currently stored in ΣPAR; the same as PREDY.

28s.description: Predicts the dependent value for a given independent value from the line LR last stored in ΣPAR: slope times x plus intercept. Without an earlier LR it returns 0.

PREDX.name: Predicted x-value
PREDX.description: Predicts the independent value for a given dependent value from the line last fitted by LR (coefficients in ΣPAR).

PREDY.name: Predicted y-value
PREDY.description: Predicts the dependent value for a given independent value from the line last fitted by LR (coefficients in ΣPAR).

PREVAL.name: Evaluate between bounds
PREVAL.description: Evaluates an expression at two bounds of the current CAS variable and returns the difference, upper value minus lower value; combined with INTVX it gives definite integrals.

examples.comment: A is the lower bound and B the upper

PREVPRIME.name: Previous prime
PREVPRIME.description: Returns the largest prime number less than the given integer.

PRLCD.name: Print display
PRLCD.description: Prints a pixel image of the whole display.
PRLCD.skip: prints to the infrared or serial printer

PRMD.name: Print modes
PRMD.description: Shows and prints the current modes: display format, binary base, angle mode, radix mark, and which of UNDO, COMMAND, LAST and the multi-line display are on.

PROMPT.description: Shows a string in the status area, then suspends the program so the user can enter or edit values on the stack; CONT resumes execution.
PROMPT.skip: halts the program and waits for the user to press CONT

PROMPTSTO.name: Prompt and store
PROMPTSTO.description: Asks the user for a value for the named variable and stores what is entered in it.
PROMPTSTO.skip: waits for the user to type a value

PROOT.name: Polynomial roots
PROOT.description: Finds all roots, real or complex, of a polynomial given as a coefficient vector ordered from the highest power down.

examples.comment: X^2 + 1 has the roots i and -i

PROPFRAC.name: Proper fraction
PROPFRAC.description: Splits an improper fraction, numeric or rational in a variable, into an integer or polynomial part plus a proper fraction.

PRST.name: Print stack
PRST.description: Prints every stack level, multi-line objects in full.
PRST.skip: prints to the infrared or serial printer

PRSTC.name: Print stack, compact
PRSTC.description: Prints the whole stack in compact form, one line per level.
PRSTC.skip: prints to the infrared or serial printer

PRUSR.name: Print user variables
PRUSR.description: Prints the current directory's variable names, in USER menu order.

PRVAR.name: Print variable
PRVAR.description: Prints one variable, or each variable in a list, showing its name and its contents.
PRVAR.skip: prints to the infrared or serial printer

PSDEV.name: Population standard deviation
PSDEV.description: Returns the population standard deviation for every column of the statistics matrix ΣDAT, treating the data as the whole population; a single column gives a real, several give a vector.

PSI.name: Polygamma
PSI.description: Evaluates the polygamma function: the n-th derivative of the digamma function at a point.

PTAYL.name: Polynomial Taylor shift
PTAYL.description: Rewrites a polynomial P around a point a: returns the polynomial Q with Q(X-a)=P(X), i.e. P's Taylor expansion at a written in powers of X.

examples.comment: (X-2)^2+7*(X-2)+11 expands back to X^2+3*X+1

PTPROP.name: Periodic table properties
PTPROP.description: Command of the periodic table library that looks up properties of chemical elements.
PTPROP.skip: argument conventions not verified; part of the periodic table application

PURGE.description: Deletes the named variable, or every variable named in a list, from the current directory; an empty subdirectory can be removed the same way.

PUSH.description: Saves the current flag settings and the current directory on an internal stack so a program can change them and restore them later with POP.

PUT.description: Replaces the element at a given position of an array or list with a new value; the position is a number or, for matrices, a {row col} list. When the target is a variable name, the variable is changed in place and nothing is returned.
PUT.stack: [array] n x → [array']; {list} n obj → {list'}; 'name' n obj →

examples.comment: Replaces element 2 with 9
Row 2, column 1 becomes 0

PUTI.name: Put and increment index
PUTI.description: Works like PUT but also returns the next position, so repeated calls fill an array or list in order; after the last element the index wraps to the first and flag -64 is set.
PUTI.stack: [array] n x → [array'] n+1; {list} n obj → {list'} n+1; 'name' n obj → 'name' n+1

examples.comment: Replaces element 1 and returns the next index, 2
After the last element the index wraps back to 1
After the last element the index wraps to 1 and flag 46 is set

28s.description: Works like PUT but also returns the next position, so repeated calls fill an array or list in order; after the last element the index wraps to 1 and flag 46 is set.
28s.stack: [array] n x → [array'] n+1; {list} n obj → {list'} n+1; 'name' n obj → 'name' n+1

PVAR.name: Population variance
PVAR.description: Returns the population variance of each column of the statistics matrix ΣDAT; a single column gives a real, several give a vector.

PVARS.name: Port variables
PVARS.description: Lists the backup objects and libraries stored in a port, and returns the port's free RAM or its memory type.

examples.comment: Port 0 holds nothing; the number is its free memory

PVIEW.name: Picture view
PVIEW.description: Shows the graphics picture on screen positioned at a given corner; an empty list instead shows it with interactive scrolling until a key is pressed.
PVIEW.skip: shows the graphics picture on screen and waits for keys

PWRFIT.name: Power curve fit
PWRFIT.description: Selects the power model y = b·x^m for later regressions, stored in ΣPAR.

PX→C.name: Pixel to complex
PX→C.description: Converts a pixel position in the graphics picture, given as a list {#x #y}, into the user-unit coordinate it represents under PPAR.

examples.comment: Pixel 0, 0 is the plot range's upper-left point
Pixel 65, 32 is the origin of the default plot window

Psi.name: Digamma
Psi.description: Evaluates the digamma function, the logarithmic derivative of the gamma function, for a real or symbolic argument.

P→R.name: Polar to rectangular
P→R.description: Converts a complex number (r,θ) in polar form to rectangular form (x,y), reading θ in the current angle mode. For a vector, elements 1 and 2 are converted and the rest kept; a real r gives (r,0).

examples.comment: Radius 2 at 90 degrees

QR.name: QR factorization
QR.description: Factors a rectangular matrix with column pivoting into an orthogonal Q, an upper-trapezoidal R and a permutation P, so that A·P = Q·R.

QUAD.name: Solve quadratic
QUAD.description: Solves a polynomial equation in a variable symbolically. The 48 models solve to second order and return one equation with the sign placeholder s1; the 49G returns a list of equations, one per root, with complex roots only when flag -103 selects complex results.

examples.comment: s1 is +1 or -1, so the roots are 2 and 1
Flag -103 selects complex mode, so the roots i and -i are found

28s.description: Solves an expression or equation for a variable from its second-order Taylor approximation, which is exact for a quadratic, and returns the solution with the sign placeholder s1.

QUOT.name: Quotient
QUOT.description: Divides one polynomial by another (Euclidean division) and returns only the quotient.

QUOTE.description: Returns its argument unchanged and unevaluated; inside an algebraic it shields a subexpression from evaluation, for example within user-defined functions.

examples.comment: A holds 5, yet the expression stays as it is

QXA.name: Quadratic form to matrix
QXA.description: Turns a quadratic form in the given variables into its symmetric matrix, leaving the variable vector beside it.

RAD.name: Radians mode
RAD.description: Selects radians as the angle unit for trigonometric functions and polar displays.

RAND.name: Random number
RAND.description: Returns the next pseudo-random real number from the calculator's generator, uniformly between 0 and 1 (exclusive); seed it with RDZ for a repeatable sequence.

examples.comment: Seed 123 gives the same number every time
The second call continues the sequence

RANK.description: Returns the rank of a matrix, i.e. how many of its rows or columns are linearly independent, found numerically.

RANM.name: Random matrix
RANM.description: Builds a matrix filled with random integers between -9 and 9, sized either by a {rows columns} list or like an existing matrix. Handy for producing test data; RDZ seeds the generator.

examples.comment: Seed 1 makes the values repeatable; 2 rows, 3 columns
Only the size of the given matrix is used

RATIO.name: Prefix divide
RATIO.description: Prefix form of division that the EquationWriter uses when building fractions; it divides like / does.

RCEQ.name: Recall equation
RCEQ.description: Recalls whatever is stored in EQ, the reserved variable that holds the current equation for plotting and the solver.

RCI.name: Multiply row by constant
RCI.description: Scales one row of a matrix (row n) by a constant factor, one of the elementary row operations used in Gaussian elimination.

examples.comment: Multiplies row 2 by 10
Multiplies row 1 by 0.5

RCIJ.name: Add multiple of row
RCIJ.description: Adds a multiple of row i to row j of a matrix, leaving row i unchanged; the elimination step of Gaussian reduction.

examples.comment: Adds -3 times row 1 to row 2
Adds -2 times row 1 to row 2

RCL.name: Recall
RCL.description: Puts a variable's value on the stack as it is, unevaluated, searching the current directory and then its parents.

RCLALARM.name: Recall alarm
RCLALARM.description: Recalls the alarm with the given index as a list { date time action repeat }.

examples.comment: Alarm 1 comes back as date, time, text and repeat 0

RCLF.name: Recall flags
RCLF.description: Returns the system and user flag settings as a two-element list of 64-bit binary integers, one bit per flag, flag 1 or -1 in the lowest bit.

examples.comment: Flags 1 and 3 set give 5 in the user flag word (1 + 4)
Masks the low three flags: 1 and 3 are set, 2 is clear

28s.description: Returns the 64 user flags as one binary integer, flag 1 in the lowest bit; with a smaller word size only the low flags come back.

RCLKEYS.name: Recall key assignments
RCLKEYS.description: Returns the current USER-mode key assignments as a list of object/key pairs, beginning with S when the built-in keys stay active.

RCLMENU.name: Recall menu number
RCLMENU.description: Returns the number of the current menu as a real number (menu.page); a custom menu gives 0.01.

examples.comment: Menu 2, page 1

RCLVX.name: Recall current variable
RCLVX.description: Returns the name of the CAS main variable, the one held in VX that many CAS commands work in by default.

RCLΣ.name: Recall statistics data
RCLΣ.description: Recalls the current statistics matrix stored in ΣDAT.

RCWS.name: Recall word size
RCWS.description: Returns the current binary integer word size (1 to 64 bits) as a real number.

RDM.name: Redimension
RDM.description: Redimensions an array to the dimensions given in a list, refilling it in row order; missing elements become zero and extra ones are dropped. A name argument redimensions the stored array in place.

examples.comment: A 2 by 2 matrix, filled row by row
A single size gives a vector; the fourth element is dropped

RDZ.name: Randomize
RDZ.description: Seeds the random number generator used by RAND with the given real; a seed of 0 picks a seed from the system clock, any other seed makes the following RAND sequence repeatable.

RE.name: Real part
RE.description: Extracts the real component of a complex value, or of every element of a complex array; a real argument comes back unchanged.

RECN.name: Receive renamed
RECN.description: Receives one file from a Kermit sender and stores it under the given name.
RECN.skip: talks over the serial or IR port

RECT.name: Rectangular mode
RECT.description: Switches the coordinate mode to rectangular, so vectors and complex numbers are entered and shown as Cartesian components (clears flag -16).

examples.comment: After SPHERE, RECT clears flag -16 and leaves -15 set

RECV.name: Receive
RECV.description: Receives one file from a Kermit sender and stores it under the name the sender gives.
RECV.skip: talks over the serial or IR port

REF.name: Row echelon form
REF.description: Reduces a matrix to row echelon form (upper triangular, leading entries 1) by Gaussian elimination.

REMAINDER.description: Divides one polynomial by another (Euclidean division) and returns only the remainder.

RENAME.description: Undocumented command of the 49G ROM library 221 related to renaming objects; its exact arguments are not confirmed here and it is not meant for direct use.
RENAME.skip: undocumented command whose argument order is not confirmed

REORDER.description: Rearranges a polynomial as powers of the given variable, ordered increasing or decreasing as the CAS power-order setting says.

REPEAT.description: Ends the test clause of a WHILE loop and starts its body; it consumes the test value and leaves the loop when that value is zero.
REPEAT.skip: part of the WHILE structure; see WHILE for an example

REPL.name: Replace
REPL.description: Overwrites part of a string, list or graphics object with another one of the same type, starting at the given position (or pixel coordinate for grobs); the length of the target does not change except where the replacement runs past its end.
REPL.stack: "str" n "new" → "str'"; {list} n {new} → {list'}; grob1 c grob2 → grob1'

examples.comment: Overwrites from the 2nd character
Overwrites from the 3rd element

RES.name: Resolution
RES.description: Sets the plotting resolution in PPAR, the step between sampled values of the independent variable; 0 means one sample per pixel column.

examples.comment: A binary integer sets the resolution in pixels

28s.description: Sets the plot resolution, the fourth item of PPAR: 1 plots a point in each pixel column, 2 in one column of two, and so on.

RESTORE.description: Replaces the whole HOME directory with what a backup object holds, given directly or as :n:name; the calculator then restarts.
RESTORE.skip: replaces HOME and restarts the calculator; see ARCHIVE

RESULTANT.description: Computes the resultant of two polynomials in the current variable, which is zero exactly when they share a common root.

examples.comment: Both have the root 1, so the result is 0

REVLIST.name: Reverse list
REVLIST.description: Returns a list with its elements in reverse order.

REWRITE.description: Opens the CAS menu or selection list of rewriting commands (expansion, collection, exponential and logarithm conversions).
REWRITE.skip: opens a menu or a selection screen

RISCH.name: Risch integration
RISCH.description: Finds an antiderivative of an expression in a given variable using the Risch algorithm.

RKF.name: Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg solve
RKF.description: Integrates an initial value problem y'=f(t,y) with the adaptive Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg method up to a final t, leaving the stored t and y variables at that point.
RKF.stack: { 't' 'y' f } tol t_final → { 't' 'y' f } tol y; { 't' 'y' f } { tol h } t_final → { 't' 'y' f } tol y

examples.comment: y' = -y with y=1 at t=0, solved to t=1 within .00001

RKFERR.name: Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg error estimate
RKFERR.description: For one Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg step of size h from the current t and y, returns the change in y and the estimated absolute error, without advancing the variables.
RKFERR.stack: { 't' 'y' f } h → { 't' 'y' f } h dy error

examples.comment: One step of size .5 from t=0, y=1

RKFSTEP.name: Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg step
RKFSTEP.description: Takes one adaptive Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg step of y'=f(t,y) from the current stored t and y, shrinking the trial step if needed to meet the tolerance, and returns the suggested next step.
RKFSTEP.stack: { 't' 'y' f } tol h → { 't' 'y' f } tol h_next t y

RL.name: Rotate left
RL.description: Rotates the bits of a binary integer one place to the left within the current word size; the bit pushed out at the top comes back in at the bottom.

examples.comment: The top bit wraps to the bottom

RLB.name: Rotate left byte
RLB.description: Rotates a binary integer left by eight bits (one byte) within the current word size, wrapping the top byte around to the bottom.

examples.comment: The top byte wraps to the bottom

RND.name: Round
RND.description: Rounds a number to n decimal places for n from 0 to 11, or to |n| significant digits for n from -1 to -11; n = 12 leaves the number as is. Works element-wise on arrays and on complex numbers.
RND.stack: x n → y; z n → z'; [array] n → [array]'

examples.comment: A negative count rounds to 3 significant digits

28s.description: Rounds a number to the current display format: n FIX rounds to n decimal places, n SCI and n ENG to n+1 significant digits, and STD leaves it unchanged. Works element-wise on complex numbers and arrays.

RNRM.name: Row norm
RNRM.description: Computes an array's row norm (also called the infinity norm): the largest sum of absolute values across any row; for a vector it is the largest absolute element.

ROLL.description: Moves the object at the given stack level up to level 1, shifting the objects above it down by one.
ROLL.stack: objn … obj1 n → objn-1 … obj1 objn

examples.comment: Rolls the 4 levels: the 1 from level 4 comes down to level 1

ROLLD.name: Roll down
ROLLD.description: Takes the object from level 1 down to the given stack level, shifting the objects in between up by one; the inverse of ROLL.
ROLLD.stack: objn … obj1 n → obj1 objn … obj2

ROMUPLOAD.name: ROM upload
ROMUPLOAD.description: Transfers the operating system to another calculator over the serial cable, for cloning or upgrading its ROM.
ROMUPLOAD.skip: talks over the serial port and waits for the receiving calculator

ROOT.description: Searches numerically for a value of a variable that makes an expression or program zero (or balances an equation), starting from one guess or a list of guesses; the root is also stored in the variable.
ROOT.stack: 'symb' 'name' guess → x; prog 'name' guess → x; 'symb' 'name' {guesses} → x

ROT.name: Rotate
ROT.description: Rotates the top three stack levels so that the third object moves to the top.
ROT.stack: obj1 obj2 obj3 → obj2 obj3 obj1

ROW+.name: Insert row
ROW+.description: Inserts a vector as a new row at position n of a matrix, shifting the following rows down; n may be one past the last row to append. On a vector it inserts a number as element n.

ROW-.name: Delete row
ROW-.description: Removes row n from a matrix and returns the shortened matrix together with the removed row as a vector. On a vector it removes and returns element n.

ROW→.name: Rows to matrix
ROW→.description: Assembles a matrix from a count and that many row vectors on the stack, the first row deepest. With plain numbers instead of vectors it makes a single column vector.

RPL>.description: Internal command of the development tools; not meant for direct use.

RR.name: Rotate right
RR.description: Rotates the bits of a binary integer one place to the right within the current word size; the lowest bit wraps around into the highest position.

examples.comment: The lowest bit wraps to the top
In an 8-bit word the lowest bit wraps to 128

RRB.name: Rotate right byte
RRB.description: Rotates a binary integer right by eight bits (one byte) within the current word size, moving the low byte up to the top.

examples.comment: In a 16-bit word the two bytes swap

RREF.name: Reduced row echelon form
RREF.description: Row-reduces a matrix by Gauss-Jordan elimination until it is in reduced row echelon form, useful for reading off the solution of an augmented system.

RREFMOD.name: Reduced row echelon form modulo
RREFMOD.description: Row-reduces a matrix to reduced echelon form using arithmetic modulo the current CAS modulus.

RRK.name: Rosenbrock and Runge-Kutta solve
RRK.description: Integrates an initial value problem y'=f(t,y) up to a final t with the Rosenbrock and Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg methods, using supplied partial derivatives of f; suited to stiff equations.
RRK.stack: { 't' 'y' f fy ft } tol t_final → { 't' 'y' f fy ft } tol y; { 't' 'y' f fy ft } { tol h } t_final → { 't' 'y' f fy ft } tol y

examples.comment: The partial derivatives of -Y, -1 and 0, extend the list

RRKSTEP.name: Rosenbrock or Runge-Kutta step
RRKSTEP.description: Takes one adaptive step of y'=f(t,y) from the stored t and y, choosing between Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg (1) and Rosenbrock (2); returns the next step size and the method it used.
RRKSTEP.stack: { 't' 'y' f fy ft } tol h last → { 't' 'y' f fy ft } tol h_next current t y

RSBERR.name: Rosenbrock error estimate
RSBERR.description: For one Rosenbrock step of size h from the current t and y, returns the change in y and the estimated absolute error, without advancing the variables.
RSBERR.stack: { 't' 'y' f fy ft } h → { 't' 'y' f fy ft } h dy error

RSD.name: Residual
RSD.description: Computes the residual B - A·Z of a linear system A·Z = B, given the right-hand side B, the coefficient matrix A and a trial solution Z; useful for checking or refining a solution.

examples.comment: Level 3 is B, level 2 is A, level 1 the trial solution Z
Z solves the system exactly, so the residual is zero

RSWP.name: Row swap
RSWP.description: Exchanges two rows of a matrix, or two elements of a vector, given their indices.

RULES.description: Brings up the menu of algebraic rearrangement rules for the subexpression selected in the EquationWriter, such as commuting, distributing or merging terms.
RULES.skip: works only inside the EquationWriter's interactive subexpression selection

R~SB.name: Real to system binary
R~SB.description: Converts a real number to a system binary integer, or a system binary back to a real; needs library 256 attached.

R→B.name: Real to binary
R→B.description: Turns a non-negative real into a binary integer, rounding to an integer first; values beyond the word size become the largest representable binary integer.

examples.comment: 10.6 is rounded to 11 first

R→C.name: Real to complex
R→C.description: Combines a real and an imaginary part into a complex number; applied to two real arrays of equal size it builds a complex array element by element.

R→D.name: Radians to degrees
R→D.description: Converts an angle in radians to degrees, independent of the current angle mode.

R→I.name: Real to integer
R→I.description: Turns a real number with no fractional part into an exact integer; applied to a symbolic expression, it converts such reals inside it.

R→P.name: Rectangular to polar
R→P.description: Converts a complex number from rectangular form (x,y) to polar form (r,θ), with the angle in the current angle mode. A real x becomes (x,0).

examples.comment: Straight up: radius 2 at 90 degrees

SAME.description: Compares two objects of any type for identity and returns 1 or 0; unlike ==, it never produces a symbolic result.

examples.comment: Different names give 0, not a symbolic result

SBRK.name: Serial break
SBRK.description: Sends a serial break signal over the serial port.

SB~B.name: System binary to binary
SB~B.description: Converts a system binary integer to a user binary integer, or a user binary integer back to a system binary; needs library 256 attached.

SCALE.description: Sets the plot ranges so that each axis has the given number of user units per 10 pixels, keeping the current centre; stored in PPAR.

examples.comment: 2 units per 10 pixels in x, 1 in y

SCALEH.name: Scale height
SCALEH.description: Multiplies the vertical extent of the plot window by a factor, keeping its center fixed; the new range is written into PPAR.

SCALEW.name: Scale width
SCALEW.description: Multiplies the horizontal extent of the plot window by a factor, keeping its center fixed; the new range is written into PPAR.

SCATRPLOT.name: Draw scatter plot
SCATRPLOT.description: Draws a scatter plot of the independent against the dependent column of ΣDAT into the graphics picture.
SCATRPLOT.skip: draws into the graphics picture and returns nothing to the stack

SCATTER.name: Scatter plot type
SCATTER.description: Selects the scatter plot type, which draws each data point of the two chosen columns of ΣDAT as a dot.

SCHUR.name: Schur decomposition
SCHUR.description: Computes the Schur decomposition A = Q·T·TRN(Q) of a square matrix: Q is orthogonal (unitary for complex input) and T is upper triangular, or block upper triangular for real matrices with complex eigenvalues.

SCI.name: Scientific mode
SCI.description: Sets scientific display: one digit before the point, the given number of decimals, and an exponent.

examples.comment: Two decimals; 1234.5 is rounded to 1.23E3

SCLΣ.name: Scale to statistics data
SCLΣ.description: Rescales the plot window in PPAR so that the data of the chosen ΣDAT columns fit for a scatter plot.

SCONJ.name: Store conjugate
SCONJ.description: Conjugates the value held in a named variable and keeps the result in that variable.

SCROLL.description: Shows an object full screen in a viewer that can be scrolled with the arrow keys.
SCROLL.skip: opens an interactive viewer that waits for keys

SDEV.name: Standard deviation
SDEV.description: Returns the sample standard deviation of every column of ΣDAT, as a real for single-column data or a vector otherwise.

SEND.description: Transfers one variable, or each variable in a list, to another Kermit device.
SEND.skip: talks over the serial or IR port

SEQ.name: Sequence
SEQ.description: Generates a list by evaluating an expression or program for each value of an index variable running from a start to an end value in a given step.
SEQ.stack: 'symb' 'name' start end step → {list}; prog 'name' start end step → {list}

examples.comment: K runs from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.25

SEQTAB.name: Sequence table
SEQTAB.description: Opens the table view of a sequence plot, listing indices with the corresponding terms.

SERIAL.description: Returns a string that identifies the ROM build of the calculator. Part of the development library.

SERIES.description: Computes a series expansion of an expression at a point to a chosen order, returning a list with the limit, an equivalent, the expansion and the error order, plus the increment variable used.

SERVER.description: Puts the calculator into Kermit server mode, waiting for commands from the other device.
SERVER.skip: talks over the serial or IR port and waits for the user

SEVAL.name: Evaluate variables
SEVAL.description: Replaces the variables of an expression that exist in the current path by their values, without evaluating the expression as a whole.

SF.name: Set flag
SF.description: Sets a flag; positive numbers address the user flags 1 to 64, negative numbers the system flags that control modes such as angle units and number formats.

examples.comment: Sets flag 3, then tests it: 1 means set

28s.description: Sets one of the 64 flags. Programs may use flags 1 to 30 freely; flags 31 to 64 control modes such as angle units, number formats and the binary word size.

SHOW.description: Expands an expression by replacing names (except the ones listed) with their variable contents until the given name appears explicitly.

examples.comment: B is replaced by its contents, X stays as a name

28s.description: Expands an expression by replacing names with their variable contents until the given name appears explicitly.

SIDENS.name: Silicon intrinsic density
SIDENS.description: Gives the intrinsic carrier density of silicon, in carriers per cubic centimetre, at a temperature in kelvins.

SIGMA.name: Discrete antiderivative
SIGMA.description: Finds a discrete antiderivative of an expression in a named variable, the summation counterpart of an indefinite integral.

SIGMAVX.name: Discrete antiderivative in the current variable
SIGMAVX.description: Finds a discrete antiderivative with respect to the current CAS variable: a function F with F(X+1)-F(X) equal to the given expression, useful for closed-form sums.

SIGN.description: For a real number gives -1, 0 or 1 according to its sign; for a complex number gives the unit vector in its direction (the number divided by its magnitude).

examples.comment: The unit vector: (3,4) divided by its length, 5

SIGNTAB.name: Sign table
SIGNTAB.description: Tabulates where a rational function in the current CAS variable changes sign, returning a list that alternates the boundary points with the sign of the function between them.

SIMP2.name: Simplify fraction
SIMP2.description: Divides two objects by their greatest common divisor, giving the reduced numerator and denominator of their ratio.

examples.comment: 12/18 reduces to 2/3: both numbers are divided by 6

SIMPLIFY.description: Applies the CAS simplification rules to an expression to bring it into a simpler equivalent form.

SIN.name: Sine
SIN.description: Sine of an angle, read in whichever angle mode is active (degrees, radians or grads); complex arguments and algebraics are accepted too.
SIN.stack: x → sin x; z → sin z; 'symb' → 'SIN(symb)'

SINCOS.name: To sines and cosines
SINCOS.description: Converts complex exponentials and logarithms in an expression into sines, cosines and arguments.

SINH.name: Hyperbolic sine
SINH.description: Computes the hyperbolic sine of a real or complex argument; symbolic arguments give a symbolic result.
SINH.stack: x → sinh x; z → sinh z; 'symb' → 'SINH(symb)'

SINV.name: Store inverse
SINV.description: Takes the reciprocal of the value held in a named variable and stores it back in place.

SIZE.description: Measures an object: the character count of a string, the element count of a list or algebraic, the dimensions of an array as a list, or the width and height of a graphics object as binary integers.

examples.comment: Rows, then columns
Counts A, B, C and the two operators

28s.description: Measures an object: the character count of a string, the element count of a list, the dimensions of an array as a list, or the number of objects in an algebraic.

SL.name: Shift left
SL.description: Logical left shift by one bit: the low bit is filled with zero and anything moving past the word size is lost; equivalent to doubling modulo the word size.

examples.comment: The highest bit falls off the end, leaving 0

SLB.name: Shift left byte
SLB.description: Moves a binary integer's bits eight places to the left (one byte), filling the low byte with zeros and dropping bits beyond the word size.

SLOPEFIELD.name: Slope field plot type
SLOPEFIELD.description: Selects the slope-field plot as the current plot type, drawing short line segments whose slopes show a first-order differential equation y'(x,y) across the view.

SNEG.name: Store negate
SNEG.description: Negates the value held in a named variable and stores it back in place.

SNRM.name: Spectral norm
SNRM.description: Spectral norm of an array: for a vector, its Euclidean length; for a matrix, its biggest singular value.

SOLVE.description: Finds the values of a variable that satisfy an equation (or make an expression zero) and returns them as a list; also accepts a vector of equations with a vector of variables. In exact mode it may return an empty list when only approximate roots exist.

SOLVEQN.name: Start equation solver
SOLVEQN.description: Loads an Equation Library set selected by subject and title numbers and starts the matching solver; the third argument says whether to show the picture first.
SOLVEQN.skip: starts the interactive solver and changes the menu and current directory variables

SOLVER.description: Opens the CAS menu of symbolic and numeric equation-solving commands.

SOLVETAB.name: Solver table
SOLVETAB.description: Opens the table view associated with the solver.

SOLVEVX.name: Solve for the current variable
SOLVEVX.description: Finds the values of the current CAS variable that satisfy an equation, or make an expression zero, and returns them.

SORT.description: Sorts a list of reals, strings, names or binary integers into ascending order; the elements must all be of one comparable type.

SPHERE.name: Spherical mode
SPHERE.description: Switches the coordinate mode to spherical, so three-element vectors are shown as radius and two angles (sets flags -15 and -16).

SQ.name: Square
SQ.description: Squares its argument; for a square matrix it returns the matrix product of the matrix with itself.

SR.name: Shift right
SR.description: Logical right shift by one bit: the top is filled with zero and the lowest bit is lost, so it halves the value rounding down.

SRAD.name: Spectral radius
SRAD.description: For a square matrix, returns its spectral radius: the largest absolute value any of its eigenvalues has.

SRB.name: Shift right byte
SRB.description: Moves a binary integer's bits eight places to the right (one byte), filling the top byte with zeros and discarding the low byte.

SRECV.name: Serial receive
SRECV.description: Reads up to n characters waiting in the serial receive buffer, returning them with 1 on success or 0 on error or timeout.

SREPL.name: String replace
SREPL.description: Searches a string for every occurrence of a substring and replaces each with another string, returning the new string and how many replacements were made.

examples.comment: Both Bs are replaced; the count 2 is on level 1
Nothing found: the string is unchanged and the count is 0

SREV.name: String reverse
SREV.description: Reverses the order of the characters in a string; needs library 256 attached.

START.description: Opens a counted loop start finish START body NEXT (or STEP) that runs the body once for each count from start to finish without exposing a loop variable. Only valid inside programs.

examples.comment: Runs the loop 5 times, doubling each time

STAT2TAB.name: Two-variable statistics table
STAT2TAB.description: Opens the table view for two-variable statistics data.

STATTAB.name: Statistics table
STATTAB.description: Opens the table view for one-variable statistics data.

STD.name: Standard mode
STD.description: Restores the standard display format, which shows numbers with all significant digits and no trailing zeros.

STEP.description: Ends a FOR or START loop, taking the increment for the counter from the stack before deciding whether to repeat.
STEP.skip: fragment of FOR ... STEP or START ... STEP; see FOR for a complete example

STEQ.name: Store equation
STEQ.description: Stores an object in the reserved variable EQ, which the plotter and the solver use as the current equation.

STIME.name: Serial timeout
STIME.description: Sets the serial transmit and receive timeout in seconds (0 to 25.4; 0 waits forever); it does not affect Kermit.

STO.name: Store
STO.description: Puts an object into a variable of the current directory, creating the variable or replacing its contents.

STO*.name: Store times
STO*.description: Multiplies what a variable holds by an object and stores the product back; the arguments may come in either order.

STO+.name: Store plus
STO+.description: Adds an object to the value held in a variable and stores the sum back; the arguments may come in either order.

28s.description: Adds a value (number or array) to what a variable holds and stores the sum back; the arguments may come in either order.

STO-.name: Store minus
STO-.description: Subtracts and stores back into a variable: with the name in level 2 it computes contents minus obj, with the name in level 1 obj minus contents.

examples.comment: A minus 1 (name in level 2)
10 minus A (name in level 1)

STO/.name: Store divide
STO/.description: Divides and stores back into a variable: with the name in level 2 it computes contents divided by obj, with the name in level 1 obj divided by contents.

examples.comment: A divided by 2 (name in level 2)
2 divided by A (name in level 1)

STOALARM.name: Store alarm
STOALARM.description: Adds an alarm to the system's alarm list and returns the new alarm's index; the argument is a time (today), a list { date time }, or a list adding an action (string to show or program to run) and a repeat interval in ticks.
STOALARM.stack: time → n; { date time } → n; { date time obj } → n; { date time obj x_repeat } → n

examples.comment: Date 1 January 2030, time 12:00, text Meet; the result is the alarm's index
Date 1 January 2030, time 9:30

STOF.name: Store flags
STOF.description: Sets all flag states from a binary integer (system flags only) or from a { #sys #user } list of binary integers, as RCLF returns them.

examples.comment: #FF0h keeps the word size and base flags set; #5h sets user flags 1 and 3
Only the system flags change: user flag 1 stays set
The binary integer 5 sets flags 1 and 3 and leaves 2 clear

28s.description: Sets all 64 flags from the bits of a binary integer, as RCLF returns it: the lowest bit is flag 1, and missing high bits clear their flags.

STOKEYS.name: Store key assignments
STOKEYS.description: Replaces or adds USER-mode key assignments from a list of object/key pairs; a leading S in the list restores the built-in key definitions first.

STORE.description: Stores a value in a named variable, like STO; kept for compatibility with the HP 40G CAS syntax.

STOVX.name: Set current variable
STOVX.description: Sets the CAS main variable, stored in VX, to the given name.

STOΣ.name: Store statistics data
STOΣ.description: Stores a matrix (one row per data point) in the reserved variable ΣDAT, making it the current statistics data.

STREAM.description: Folds a list with a two-argument program: it applies the program to the first two elements, then to that result together with the third, and so on, leaving the final value.

examples.comment: Multiplies the elements one after another
Keeps the larger of each pair

STRM.description: Internal command of the ROM; not meant for direct use.

STR→.name: String to object
STR→.description: Treats the string as command-line text: compiles it and evaluates the result, so it can create objects or run commands from text. Superseded by OBJ→ but still accepted.

28s.description: Treats the string as command-line text: compiles it and evaluates the result, so it can create objects or run commands from text.

STURM.name: Sturm sequence
STURM.description: Computes the Sturm sequence of a polynomial, used to count its real roots in an interval.

STURMAB.name: Sturm root count
STURMAB.description: Uses the Sturm sequence of a polynomial to count its real roots between two bounds; it also returns the polynomial's value at the lower bound.

examples.comment: One root between 0 and 2; the polynomial is -2 at 0
No real root between 0 and 2

STWS.name: Set word size
STWS.description: Sets the word size used for binary integer arithmetic and display, from 1 to 64 bits; values outside that range are clamped.

examples.comment: With 8 bits, 1FF is cut to FF

28s.description: Sets the word size used for binary integer arithmetic and display, from 1 to 64 bits; values outside that range are clamped.

SUB.name: Subset
SUB.description: Extracts the part of a string or list between two positions, both inclusive; for a graphics object it cuts out the rectangle between two corner coordinates.
SUB.stack: "str" n1 n2 → "sub"; {list} n1 n2 → {sub}; grob c1 c2 → grob'

examples.comment: The 2nd to 4th character
The 2nd and 3rd elements

28s.description: Extracts the part of a string or list between two positions, both inclusive.

SUBST.name: Substitute
SUBST.description: Replaces a variable in an expression by a value or another expression, given as an equation such as X=2, without evaluating the result further.

SUBTMOD.name: Subtract modulo
SUBTMOD.description: Subtracts the second expression or integer from the first and reduces the result modulo the current CAS modulus.

SVD.name: Singular value decomposition
SVD.description: Computes the singular value decomposition A = U·S·V of a rectangular matrix, returning the orthogonal factors U and V and the singular values as a vector.

SVL.name: Singular values
SVL.description: Computes the singular values of any rectangular matrix and returns them as a vector in decreasing order.

SWAP.description: Exchanges the top two stack objects.

SYLVESTER.name: Sylvester's law of inertia
SYLVESTER.description: For a symmetric matrix A, finds a diagonal D, returned as the vector of its diagonal, and a matrix P such that A equals the transpose of P times D times P.

SYSEVAL.name: Evaluate system object
SYSEVAL.description: Executes the system object found at the given ROM or RAM address, bypassing all argument checks. Only meant for addresses published for a specific ROM version; a wrong address can corrupt memory.
SYSEVAL.skip: jumps into an arbitrary system address; results depend on the ROM version and a wrong address can crash or clear memory

SYST2MAT.name: System to matrix
SYST2MAT.description: Converts a system of linear equations and its list of unknowns into the augmented coefficient matrix of the system.

examples.comment: The last column holds the constants moved to the left side: -3 and -1

S~N.name: String to name
S~N.description: Converts a string into a global name with the same characters, or a name back into a string. Part of the development library, which must be attached first.

S→H.name: String to hex
S→H.description: Converts a string to the hexadecimal digits of its characters in nibble order, two digits per character; needs library 256 attached.

examples.comment: A is 41 and B is 42 in hexadecimal, each with its two digits in reverse order

TABVAL.name: Table of values
TABVAL.description: Evaluates an expression in the current variable at each value of a list, returning the expression and a list pairing the inputs with the results.

TABVAR.name: Variation table
TABVAR.description: Works out the variation table of a rational function in the current CAS variable: where it rises or falls and its values at the turning points, with a picture of the table.
TABVAR.skip: shows the variation table in a viewer that waits for a key

TAIL.description: Returns a list without its first element, or a string without its first character.

TAN.name: Tangent
TAN.description: Tangent of an angle in the current angle mode, for reals, complex numbers and algebraics.
TAN.stack: x → tan x; z → tan z; 'symb' → 'TAN(symb)'

TAN2CS2.name: Tangent to double-angle sine and cosine
TAN2CS2.description: Rewrites tangents in an expression in terms of the sine and cosine of the doubled angle.

TAN2SC.name: Tangent to sine over cosine
TAN2SC.description: Replaces each tangent in an expression by the quotient of the sine and cosine of the same argument.

TAN2SC2.name: Tangent to double-angle sine and cosine
TAN2SC2.description: Replaces each tangent in an expression by an expression in the sine and cosine of the doubled argument.

TANH.name: Hyperbolic tangent
TANH.description: Computes the hyperbolic tangent of a real or complex argument; symbolic arguments give a symbolic result.
TANH.stack: x → tanh x; z → tanh z; 'symb' → 'TANH(symb)'

TAYLOR0.name: Taylor polynomial at 0
TAYLOR0.description: Expands an expression into a Taylor polynomial around 0 in the current CAS variable, to relative order 4.

TAYLR.name: Taylor polynomial
TAYLR.description: Computes the Taylor polynomial of an expression about zero in a variable, up to a given order.

TCHEBYCHEFF.name: Chebyshev polynomial
TCHEBYCHEFF.description: Builds the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind of degree n in the current CAS variable, as an exact symbolic expression.

TCOLLECT.name: Trigonometric collect
TCOLLECT.description: Linearizes a trigonometric expression and then combines sines and cosines of the same angle into compact terms.

TDELTA.name: Temperature delta
TDELTA.description: Subtracts an initial temperature from a final one and returns the difference as a temperature increment, so offset scales such as °C and °F are handled correctly; with units the result carries the first argument's unit.
TDELTA.stack: x y → x_delta; x_unit1 y_unit2 → x_unit1delta

examples.comment: 100 °C minus 50 °F is a difference of 90 °C

TEACH.name: Teaching examples
TEACH.description: Copies a set of programming, plotting and solver demonstration programs from ROM into a new EXAMPLES directory under HOME.
TEACH.skip: fills HOME with a ROM examples directory; listed among the interactive teaching commands

TESTS.description: Menu-entry word of the CAS that brings up the menu of test and comparison commands.

TEVAL.name: Timed evaluation
TEVAL.description: Evaluates an object and also returns how long the evaluation took, in seconds, tagged with s.

TEXPAND.name: Transcendental expand
TEXPAND.description: Expands trigonometric, hyperbolic, exponential and logarithmic functions of sums and multiples into functions of the single terms.

TEXT.description: Switches the screen back from the graphics picture to the normal stack display.
TEXT.skip: only changes which screen is shown

THEN.description: Separates the test clause from the clause that runs when the test is true in IF, IFERR and CASE structures; it consumes the test value.
THEN.skip: part of the IF / IFERR / CASE structures; see IF for an example

28s.description: Ends the test clause of an IF structure and takes the test value from the stack, or ends the trap clause of an IFERR structure. The clause after it runs when the test is true or an error occurred.

TI1M.name: t interval, one mean
TI1M.description: Internal routine of the statistics confidence-interval application; the name points to a Student t interval for one mean. Not meant for direct use.
TI1M.skip: internal routine of the statistics interval forms with undocumented arguments

TI2M.name: t interval, two means
TI2M.description: Internal routine of the statistics confidence-interval application; the name points to a Student t interval for the gap between two means. Not meant for direct use.
TI2M.skip: internal routine of the statistics interval forms with undocumented arguments

TICKS.name: System clock ticks
TICKS.description: Returns the system clock as a binary integer counting ticks of 1/8192 second; differences of two readings time an operation.

TIME.description: Returns the current time of the system clock as a real number in HH.MMSSss form, 24-hour.

examples.comment: After setting 12:30 the clock has run a few seconds

TINC.name: Temperature increment
TINC.description: Raises a temperature by an increment, treating the second argument as a temperature difference rather than an absolute temperature; with units the result carries the first argument's unit.
TINC.stack: x y_delta → x'; x_unit1 y_unit2 → x_unit1'

examples.comment: A rise of 15 K is a rise of 15 °C
A rise of 10 °C is 18 °F, so 68 becomes 86

TLIN.name: Trigonometric linearize
TLIN.description: Linearizes a trigonometric expression, turning products and powers of sines and cosines into sums of sines and cosines of multiple angles.

TLINE.name: Toggle line
TLINE.description: Draws a line between two points of the graphics picture by inverting each pixel it crosses, so drawing it twice removes it.
TLINE.skip: draws into the graphics picture and returns nothing to the stack

TMENU.name: Temporary menu
TMENU.description: Shows a temporary custom menu built from a list of names, commands or { label action } pairs, or selects a built-in menu by number, without changing the CST variable.

examples.comment: A custom menu reads as .01

TOT.name: Total
TOT.description: Returns the column sums of ΣDAT, as a real for single-column data or a vector otherwise.

TRACE.description: Sums the main diagonal elements of a square matrix (its trace).

TRAN.name: Transpose
TRAN.description: Transposes a matrix, swapping rows and columns without conjugating complex entries.

TRANSIO.name: I/O translation
TRANSIO.description: Selects the character translation used for ASCII transfers and serial printing (0 to 3) and stores it in IOPAR.

examples.comment: The translation code, 2, is the last element of IOPAR

TRIG.name: Trigonometric simplify
TRIG.description: Simplifies trigonometric expressions using sin²+cos²=1 and rewrites trigonometric terms consistently.

TRIGCOS.name: Trigonometric simplify to cosines
TRIGCOS.description: Simplifies a trigonometric expression using sin²+cos²=1, preferring cosine terms in the result.

TRIGO.name: Trigonometry menu
TRIGO.description: Opens the CAS menu of trigonometric rewriting commands.

TRIGSIN.name: Trigonometric simplify to sines
TRIGSIN.description: Simplifies a trigonometric expression using sin²+cos²=1, preferring sine terms in the result.

TRIGTAN.name: Trigonometric rewrite to tangents
TRIGTAN.description: Rewrites the sines and cosines in a trigonometric expression in terms of tangents.

TRN.name: Transpose
TRN.description: Transposes a matrix, swapping rows and columns; complex matrices are also conjugated. A name argument transposes the stored matrix in place.

examples.comment: Complex entries are conjugated: (1,1) becomes (1,-1)

TRNC.name: Truncate
TRNC.description: Truncates a number to n decimal places, or to |n| significant digits when n is negative, cutting off the remaining digits instead of rounding.
TRNC.stack: x n → y; z n → z'; [array] n → [array]'

examples.comment: A negative count keeps 3 significant digits

TRUNC.name: Truncate series
TRUNC.description: Cuts a series expansion short by dropping every term whose order is at least that of the second argument.

TRUTH.name: Truth plot type
TRUTH.description: Selects the truth plot type, which turns on every pixel where the comparison or logical expression in EQ is true.

TSIMP.name: Transcendental simplify
TSIMP.description: Simplifies an expression containing exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions by rewriting them through complex exponentials.

TSTR.name: Date and time string
TSTR.description: Formats a date and a time as a readable string with weekday, date and time, following the date and clock format flags.

examples.comment: 1 January 2030 at 12:30
4 July 1991 at 18:45:12, shown on a 12-hour clock

TVARS.name: Typed variables
TVARS.description: Lists the variables in the directory you are in whose contents have the given object type, or any type from a list of types.

examples.comment: Type 0 is real: only A is listed
Types 0 (real) and 2 (string)

TVM.name: Time value of money
TVM.description: Opens the time-value-of-money solver menu, where loan and savings variables (PV, PMT, FV, N, I%YR, PYR) are entered and solved for.
TVM.skip: only displays the interactive TVM solver menu

TVMBEG.name: Payments at beginning of period
TVMBEG.description: Switches TVM calculations to payments made at the start of every period (annuity due) by setting flag -14.

TVMEND.name: Payments at end of period
TVMEND.description: Switches TVM calculations to payments made when every period ends (ordinary annuity, the default) by clearing flag -14.

TVMROOT.name: Time value of money root
TVMROOT.description: Solves for the named TVM variable (N, I%YR, PV, PMT or FV) from the values stored in the other TVM variables, honouring the payment mode in flag -14.

examples.comment: Loan of 10000, 36 payments, 6% a year, 12 payments a year; solves PMT

TYPE.description: Returns a number identifying the kind of object in level 1, for example 0 for a real, 1 for complex, 2 for a string, 5 for a list, 6 for a global name, 9 for an algebraic and 10 for a binary integer. Programs use it to branch on argument type.

UBASE.name: Convert to SI base units
UBASE.description: Rewrites a unit object in SI base units, multiplying out prefixes and derived units.

UFACT.name: Factor unit
UFACT.description: Factors the unit of level 1 out of the unit expression in level 2, so the result is expressed partly in that unit.

examples.comment: Factors N out of the joule

UFL1→MINIF.name: UFL1 font to minifont
UFL1→MINIF.description: Converts a font set in UFL1 (Universal Font Library) format into a minifont object, given the font set and a font identifier.
UFL1→MINIF.skip: needs a UFL1 font set object, which cannot be typed on the command line

UNASSIGN.description: CAS command that removes the values bound to the named variables, so the names act again as free symbols in later computations.

UNASSUME.description: Removes assumptions recorded for a variable, returning it to an unconstrained CAS variable; kept from the HP 40G CAS.

UNBIND.description: Discards the local variables most recently created by LOCAL.

UNPICK.description: Takes an object and a level number n and puts the object in place of whatever sits at level n of the remaining stack.

examples.comment: 99 replaces the object on level 2, the 2

UNROT.name: Unrotate
UNROT.description: Rotates the top three stack levels the opposite way to ROT: the object on level 1 moves to level 3 and the other two move up.
UNROT.stack: x y z → z x y

UNTIL.description: Ends the body of a DO loop and starts its test clause, whose result decides at END whether the loop repeats.
UNTIL.skip: part of the DO structure; see DO for an example

UPDIR.name: Up directory
UPDIR.description: Moves one level up the directory tree towards HOME, so the enclosing directory becomes current. In HOME it has no effect.

UTPC.name: Upper chi-square distribution
UTPC.description: Gives the upper-tail probability of the chi-square distribution with n degrees of freedom: the chance that such a variable exceeds x.

examples.comment: 5 degrees of freedom, upper tail beyond 11.07

UTPF.name: Upper F distribution
UTPF.description: Gives the upper-tail probability of the F (Snedecor) distribution with n1 numerator and n2 denominator degrees of freedom: the chance that such a variable exceeds x.

examples.comment: 5 and 10 degrees of freedom, value 3.33

UTPN.name: Upper normal distribution
UTPN.description: Gives the upper-tail probability of the normal distribution with mean m and variance v: the chance that such a variable exceeds x.

examples.comment: Mean 0, variance 1, value 1.96
Mean 100, variance 225, so 115 is one standard deviation above the mean

UTPT.name: Upper Student's t distribution
UTPT.description: Gives the upper-tail probability of Student's t distribution with n degrees of freedom: the chance that such a variable exceeds x.

examples.comment: 10 degrees of freedom
At 0 the upper tail is half

UVAL.name: Unit value
UVAL.description: Strips the unit from a unit object and returns the bare number.

VANDERMONDE.name: Vandermonde matrix
VANDERMONDE.description: Builds the n×n Vandermonde matrix for a list of n values: each row holds successive powers 0 to n-1 of one value.

VAR.name: Variance
VAR.description: Computes the sample variance of each column of the statistics matrix ΣDAT, as a real for one column or a vector for several.

VARS.name: Variables
VARS.description: Lists the names of every variable in the directory you are in, in menu order.

VER.name: CAS version
VER.description: Returns the version of the computer algebra system, encoded as a real number that includes its release date.

VERSION.description: Returns two strings identifying the ROM: the version label and the copyright notice.

VISIT.description: Opens the contents of a named variable in the command-line editor and stores the edited result back in that variable.
VISIT.skip: opens an interactive editor and waits for the user

VISITB.name: Visit in best editor
VISITB.description: Opens the contents of a named variable in the editor best suited to its type and stores the edited result back in that variable.
VISITB.skip: opens an interactive editor and waits for the user

VPOTENTIAL.name: Vector potential
VPOTENTIAL.description: Finds a vector field whose curl equals the given divergence-free field in three variables, the vector potential of that field.

VTYPE.name: Variable type
VTYPE.description: Looks up a variable by name and reports the object type number of its contents, or -1 when no such variable exists.

V→.name: Vector to stack
V→.description: Splits a vector into its elements on the stack. Two- and three-element vectors come out in the current coordinate mode (rectangular, polar or spherical); longer vectors always give their raw elements.
V→.stack: [x y] → x y; [x y z] → x y z; [array] → x1 ... xn

examples.comment: In cylindrical mode a 2-element vector splits into radius and angle (not on the 48SX)

WAIT.description: Pauses execution for the given number of seconds. With 0 (or a negative value) it instead waits for a keypress and returns that key's row-column code.

28s.description: Pauses a program for the given number of seconds.

WHILE.description: Opens a pre-tested loop WHILE test REPEAT body END: the test clause runs first and the body repeats for as long as the test leaves a nonzero value. Only valid inside programs.

examples.comment: Doubles the value while it is below 100

WIREFRAME.name: Wireframe plot type
WIREFRAME.description: Selects the wireframe 3D surface plot as the current plot type by putting WIREFRAME into the plot parameters in PPAR.

WSLOG.name: Warmstart log
WSLOG.description: Returns the warmstart log as four strings, the newest last, each holding a cause code and the time stamp of a recent system restart. Helps diagnose why the calculator reset itself.

XCOL.name: Independent column
XCOL.description: Chooses which column of ΣDAT serves as the independent variable for the two-variable statistics, recorded in ΣPAR.

examples.comment: Column 2 becomes the x column, so ΣX adds up that column

XGET.name: XModem get
XGET.description: Fetches a named variable from an XModem server on the other end of the serial link and stores it in the current directory.

XLIB~.name: Library command conversion
XLIB~.description: Converts between a library command reference (XLIB name) and its library and command numbers, in either direction. Part of the development library.
XLIB~.stack: n1 n2 → xlib; xlib → n1 n2

examples.comment: Library 788, command 1

XMIT.name: Serial transmit
XMIT.description: Sends a string over the serial port without Kermit, returning 1 on success or the unsent part and 0.

XNUM.name: To approximate number
XNUM.description: Turns an exact object, or every object of a list, into its approximate (floating point) value.

XOR.name: Exclusive OR
XOR.description: Bitwise exclusive OR of two binary integers; for reals it returns 1 when exactly one of the two values is non-zero, else 0. Symbolic arguments give a symbolic expression.

examples.comment: Binary 1100 XOR 1010 gives 0110

XPON.name: Exponent
XPON.description: Returns the power-of-ten exponent of a real number as it would appear in scientific notation.

examples.comment: 4.2E-4 has the exponent -4

XPUT.name: XModem put
XPUT.description: Sends a named variable to an XModem server on the other end of the serial link.

XQ.name: To exact rational
XQ.description: Turns an approximate number, or each number of a list, into the nearest exact rational or simple exact expression.

XRECV.name: XModem receive
