XRECV.description: Receives an object over the serial link using the XModem protocol and stores it under the given name.
XRECV.skip: transfers data over the serial port

XRNG.name: x-axis range
XRNG.description: Sets the horizontal plot range in PPAR to the given minimum and maximum, in user units.

XROOT.name: xth root of y
XROOT.description: Takes the root of index x (level 1) of the value y (level 2). A negative y with an odd integer index gives the real negative root.

XSEND.name: XModem send
XSEND.description: Sends a variable to another device over the serial link using the XModem protocol.
XSEND.skip: transfers data over the serial port

XSERV.name: XModem server
XSERV.description: Puts the calculator into XModem server mode so a computer can send and fetch variables over the serial link.
XSERV.skip: runs a serial-port server and waits for the host

XVOL.name: x volume
XVOL.description: Sets the left and right x bounds of the view volume used by 3D plot types, storing them in the reserved variable VPAR (created with defaults if missing).

examples.comment: Sets entries 1 and 2 of VPAR, the x bounds

XXRNG.name: x range of input plane
XXRNG.description: Sets the x extent of the input plane (the domain) that GRIDMAP and PARSURFACE plots sample, recording it in the reserved variable VPAR.

examples.comment: Sets entries 7 and 8 of VPAR

YCOL.name: Dependent column
YCOL.description: Chooses which column of ΣDAT serves as the dependent variable for the two-variable statistics, recorded in ΣPAR.

examples.comment: Column 1 becomes the y column, so ΣY adds up that column

YRNG.name: y-axis range
YRNG.description: Sets the vertical plot range in PPAR to the given minimum and maximum, in user units.

YSLICE.name: Y-slice plot type
YSLICE.description: Selects the y-slice plot as the current plot type, drawing a surface z(x,y) as a series of cross sections taken at successive y values.

YVOL.name: y volume
YVOL.description: Sets the near and far y bounds (depth) of the 3D view volume, storing them in the reserved variable VPAR.

examples.comment: Sets entries 3 and 4 of VPAR, the depth

YYRNG.name: y range of input plane
YYRNG.description: Sets the y extent of the input plane (the domain) that GRIDMAP and PARSURFACE plots sample, recording it in the reserved variable VPAR.

examples.comment: Sets entries 9 and 10 of VPAR

ZEROS.description: Returns the zeros of an expression in one variable, each listed once without multiplicity; exact or approximate depending on the CAS mode.

ZFACTOR.name: Gas compressibility Z factor
ZFACTOR.description: Computes the gas compressibility factor z from the reduced temperature (1.05 to 3) and reduced pressure (0 to 30), for real-gas corrections to the ideal gas law.

ZI1M.name: Z interval, one mean
ZI1M.description: Internal routine of the statistics confidence-interval application; the name points to a Z interval for one mean. Not meant for direct use.
ZI1M.skip: internal routine of the statistics interval forms with undocumented arguments

ZI1P.name: Z interval, one proportion
ZI1P.description: Internal routine of the statistics confidence-interval application; the name points to a Z interval for one proportion. Not meant for direct use.
ZI1P.skip: internal routine of the statistics interval forms with undocumented arguments

ZI2M.name: Z interval, two means
ZI2M.description: Internal routine of the statistics confidence-interval application; the name points to a Z interval for the gap between two means. Not meant for direct use.
ZI2M.skip: internal routine of the statistics interval forms with undocumented arguments

ZI2P.name: Z interval, two proportions
ZI2P.description: Internal routine of the statistics confidence-interval application; the name points to a Z interval for the gap between two proportions. Not meant for direct use.
ZI2P.skip: internal routine of the statistics interval forms with undocumented arguments

ZT1M.name: Z test, one mean
ZT1M.description: Internal routine of the statistics hypothesis-test application; the name points to a Z test on one mean. Not meant for direct use.
ZT1M.skip: internal routine of the statistics test forms with undocumented arguments

ZT1P.name: Z test, one proportion
ZT1P.description: Internal routine of the statistics hypothesis-test application; the name points to a Z test on one proportion. Not meant for direct use.
ZT1P.skip: internal routine of the statistics test forms with undocumented arguments

ZT1U.description: Internal routine of the statistics hypothesis-test application; not meant for direct use.
ZT1U.skip: internal routine of the statistics test forms with undocumented arguments

ZT2M.name: Z test, two means
ZT2M.description: Internal routine of the statistics hypothesis-test application; the name points to a Z test comparing two means. Not meant for direct use.
ZT2M.skip: internal routine of the statistics test forms with undocumented arguments

ZT2P.name: Z test, two proportions
ZT2P.description: Internal routine of the statistics hypothesis-test application; the name points to a Z test comparing two proportions. Not meant for direct use.
ZT2P.skip: internal routine of the statistics test forms with undocumented arguments

ZT2U.description: Internal routine of the statistics hypothesis-test application; not meant for direct use.
ZT2U.skip: internal routine of the statistics test forms with undocumented arguments

ZVOL.name: z volume
ZVOL.description: Sets the lower and upper z bounds (height) of the 3D view volume, storing them in the reserved variable VPAR.

examples.comment: Sets entries 5 and 6 of VPAR, the height

^.name: Power
^.description: Raises level 2 to the power in level 1. A negative real base with a fractional exponent gives a complex result; symbolic arguments give an algebraic.
^.stack: x y → x^y; z1 z2 → z1^z2; 'symb' y → 'symb^y'

examples.comment: The square root of -8, so the result is complex

_.name: Attach unit
_.description: The unit attachment operator: binds a number to a unit expression, as in 3_m. On the stack it combines a value with the unit given in level 1.

asm.name: Assemble
asm.description: Entry point of the MASD assembler library: assembles a string of source code into an object.

dB.name: Decibel
dB.description: The decibel, a dimensionless logarithmic unit for ratios such as power or sound level; it does not convert to other units.

e.name: Euler's number
e.description: Returns the base of natural logarithms, either as the symbol 'e' or, when numeric results or numeric constants are selected, as the real 2.71828182846.

er.name: Assembly errors
er.description: Error browser of the MASD assembler library, used after an assembly fails to step through the reported errors.
er.skip: opens an interactive error browser for the assembler

gmol.name: Gram-mole
gmol.description: The gram-mole unit of amount of substance, equal to one mole; used as a unit in unit objects such as 2._gmol.

i.name: Imaginary unit
i.description: Returns the imaginary unit, either as the symbol 'i' or, when evaluated numerically, as the complex number (0,1).

lbmol.name: Pound-mole
lbmol.description: The pound-mole unit of amount of substance, the amount whose mass in pounds equals the molecular weight (about 453.59 moles).

lim.name: Limit
lim.description: Computes the limit of an expression as a variable approaches a point, given as an equation such as X=0 (a bare name means the point 0).

qr.name: QR factorization
qr.description: Factors a matrix exactly as Q times R, where Q is orthogonal and R is upper triangular, using the CAS.

rpm.name: Revolutions per minute
rpm.description: The revolutions-per-minute unit of rotational frequency, one sixtieth of a hertz.

rref.name: Reduced row echelon form
rref.description: Row-reduces a matrix until it is in reduced row echelon form and also returns the pivots used, as a list.

|.name: Where
|.description: Substitutes values or expressions for names inside an expression, given as name/value pairs in a list; also usable as the infix operator in algebraic form.

examples.comment: X is replaced by 2 and Y by 3

«.description: Opening delimiter of a program object; everything up to the matching » is kept unevaluated as one program.
«.skip: a delimiter of program source, not a command that runs on its own

».description: Closing delimiter of a program object, typed to end the program started by «.
».skip: a delimiter of program source, not a command that runs on its own

ΔLIST.name: List differences
ΔLIST.description: Returns the list of differences between successive elements of a list of at least two numbers.

ΠLIST.name: List product
ΠLIST.description: Multiplies together all elements of a list.

Σ.name: Summation
Σ.description: Sums an expression over an integer index running from a start value to an end value. Symbolic limits leave the sum as an algebraic.

examples.comment: The sum of N^2 for N from 1 to 10

Σ+.name: Add data point
Σ+.description: Adds a row (or rows) to ΣDAT, creating it if needed: a real for one-variable data, a vector or several reals for one row, or a matrix for several rows.

examples.comment: Two single values make a one-column matrix
Adds a fourth data row, so NΣ gives 4

28s.description: Appends data to the statistics matrix ΣDAT, creating it if needed: a real for one-column data, a vector for one row, or a matrix for several rows.

Σ-.name: Remove data point
Σ-.description: Removes the last data point (row) from ΣDAT and returns it, a real for one-column data or a vector otherwise. Useful for correcting a wrong entry.

ΣLINE.name: Regression line
ΣLINE.description: Returns the fitted line from ΣPAR as an algebraic in the independent variable, ready for plotting or evaluation.

ΣLIST.name: List sum
ΣLIST.description: Adds up all elements of a list.

ΣX.name: Sum of x
ΣX.description: Adds up the independent-column entries of ΣDAT.

ΣX*Y.name: Sum of x times y
ΣX*Y.description: Multiplies each independent value in ΣDAT by its matching dependent value and returns the total.

ΣX2.name: Sum of x squared
ΣX2.description: Sums the squared entries of the independent-variable (XCOL) column of the statistics matrix ΣDAT.

ΣXY.name: Sum of x times y
ΣXY.description: Sums the products, row by row, of the two ΣDAT columns that XCOL and YCOL choose.

ΣX^2.name: Sum of x squared
ΣX^2.description: Squares each independent-column entry of ΣDAT and returns the total.

ΣY.name: Sum of y
ΣY.description: Adds up the dependent-column entries of ΣDAT.

ΣY2.name: Sum of y squared
ΣY2.description: Sums the squared entries of the dependent-variable (YCOL) column of the statistics matrix ΣDAT.

ΣY^2.name: Sum of y squared
ΣY^2.description: Squares each dependent-column entry of ΣDAT and returns the total.

π.name: Pi
π.description: Returns the constant pi, either as the symbol 'π' or, when numeric results or numeric constants are selected, as the 12-digit real 3.14159265359.

↑MATCH.name: Match and replace, bottom up
↑MATCH.description: Rewrites an expression with a pattern and replacement (optionally a condition), matching subexpressions from the innermost outward; & names are wildcards. Returns the result and 1 if anything changed, else 0.

examples.comment: Rewritten by distributing; the 1 reports a match

→.name: Create local variables
→.description: Creates local variables: it takes values from the stack, binds them to the following names, and evaluates the program or algebraic that follows with those names defined.

examples.comment: Binds 3 to a and 4 to b

→A.name: Object address
→A.description: Returns the memory address of an object as a binary integer; needs library 256 attached.
→A.skip: returns a raw memory address that depends on memory layout

→ALG.name: Stack to algebraic
→ALG.description: Gathers n objects from the stack, with their count in level 1, into an algebraic object without checking that the result is well formed; needs library 256 attached.

→ARRY.name: Stack to array
→ARRY.description: Gathers stack objects into an array: with a count it builds a vector, with a list of row and column counts a matrix filled row by row.
→ARRY.stack: x1 … xn n → [vector]; x11 … xnm {n m} → [[matrix]]

examples.comment: A 2 by 2 matrix: the list gives rows and columns

→CD.name: Hex string to code object
→CD.description: Turns a string of hexadecimal digits into a code object containing those nibbles, without running it; needs library 256 attached.

→COL.name: Matrix to columns
→COL.description: Splits a matrix into its columns, pushing each column as a vector followed by the column count. Applied to a vector, it pushes the elements and their count.

→DATE.name: Set date
→DATE.description: Sets the system clock's date from a real number written in the active date format (MM.DDYYYY by default).

examples.comment: 29 February 1992, a leap day

→DIAG.name: Matrix diagonal to vector
→DIAG.description: Extracts the main diagonal of a matrix, square or rectangular, as a vector.

→FONT.name: Set system font
→FONT.description: Makes a font object the system font used to show the stack and the command line.

→GROB.name: To graphics object
→GROB.description: Renders any object as a graphics object in a chosen font size (1 small, 2 medium, 3 large); size 0 draws algebraics the way the EquationWriter shows them.

→H.name: To hex
→H.description: Converts any object to a string of hexadecimal digits giving its nibbles in memory order; needs library 256 attached.

→HEADER.name: Set header size
→HEADER.description: Sets how many lines, from 0 to 2, the status header above the stack occupies.

→HMS.name: Decimal to hours-minutes-seconds
→HMS.description: Converts a decimal number of hours (or degrees) to HH.MMSS form.

examples.comment: 1.5 hours is 1h30m
2.7525 hours is 2h45m09s

→KEYTIME.name: Set key debounce time
→KEYTIME.description: Sets the keyboard debounce time, the delay in clock ticks the calculator waits before accepting another key press.

→LANGUAGE.name: Set language
→LANGUAGE.description: Chooses the language of system messages by number: 0 for English, 1 for French, 2 for Spanish.

→LCD.name: Graphics object to display
→LCD.description: Shows a graphics object on the screen, placing its top-left corner at the top-left of the display.
→LCD.skip: writes to the screen and returns nothing to the stack

28s.name: String to display
28s.description: Shows a string as graphics: each character code becomes a column of eight pixels, drawn from the display's top-left corner. 548 characters fill the screen.

→LIST.name: Stack to list
→LIST.description: Collects a given count of stack objects into a list, the deepest of them becoming the first element.

examples.comment: A count of 0 gives the empty list

→LST.name: Stack to list
→LST.description: Gathers n objects from the stack, with their count in level 1, into a list; needs library 256 attached.

→MINIFONT.name: Set minifont
→MINIFONT.description: Installs a font object as the minifont, the small font used for menu labels and compact display text.

→NDISP.name: Set number of stack lines
→NDISP.description: Sets the number of lines the stack display uses for showing objects.

→NUM.name: To number
→NUM.description: Evaluates an object fully to a number, replacing symbolic constants such as π and e by their numeric values and variables by their contents.

→PRG.name: Stack to program
→PRG.description: Gathers n objects from the stack, with their count in level 1, into a program; needs library 256 attached.

→Q.name: To quotient
→Q.description: Turns a real number into the algebraic fraction that best approximates it at the current display precision.

→Qπ.name: To quotient times π
→Qπ.description: Approximates a real number as a fraction, or as a fraction times π when that gives a simpler result, and returns it as an algebraic; also works on each number in an expression.

→RAM.name: Copy to RAM
→RAM.description: Replaces an object that lives in ROM, or refers to ROM, by a full copy in RAM; objects already in RAM come back unchanged. Needs library 256 attached.

→ROW.name: Matrix to rows
→ROW.description: Splits a matrix into its rows, pushing each row as a vector followed by the row count. Applied to a vector, it pushes the individual elements and their count.

→S2.name: To System RPL source
→S2.description: Disassembles an object into a string of System RPL source that ASM can assemble again. Part of the development library.

→STR.name: To string
→STR.description: Converts any object to a string showing how it is displayed, using the current number format for reals.

→TAG.name: Stack to tag
→TAG.description: Attaches a label to an object, producing a tagged object; the tag can be given as a string or a name.

→TIME.name: Set time
→TIME.description: Sets the system clock's time from a real number in 24-hour HH.MMSS form.

→UNIT.name: To unit object
→UNIT.description: Builds a unit object from a plain number and a unit object, attaching the units of the second to the first; whatever number the unit object carries is ignored. Useful in programs that compute a bare value and then label it.

→V2.name: To 2-element vector
→V2.description: Combines two reals into a two-element vector, read as rectangular or polar coordinates according to the current mode; when flag -19 is set it builds a complex number instead.

→V3.name: To 3-element vector
→V3.description: Combines three reals into a three-element vector, interpreting them as rectangular, cylindrical or spherical coordinates according to the current mode.

↓MATCH.name: Match and replace, top down
↓MATCH.description: Rewrites an expression with a pattern and replacement (optionally a condition), matching from the whole expression inward; & names are wildcards. Returns the result and 1 if anything changed, else 0.

examples.comment: Rewritten by distributing; the 1 reports a match

∂.name: Derivative
∂.description: Differentiates an expression by the named variable. The result is symbolic, or a number when the variable already holds a value.

√.name: Square root
√.description: Gives the principal square root. A negative real yields a complex result, and units and algebraics are handled as well.

28s.description: Gives the principal square root. A negative real yields a complex result, and algebraics give a symbolic result.

∞.name: Infinity
∞.description: Puts the symbolic constant for unsigned infinity on the stack, for use in limits, integrals and series.

examples.comment: The limit of 1/X as X goes to infinity

∫.name: Integral
∫.description: Integrates an expression over a variable between two limits. It integrates symbolically when it can; with numeric evaluation it integrates numerically, to an accuracy set by the display format.

examples.comment: 0 to 1 to within .00001; the second value is the error estimate

28s.description: Integrates an expression. With a variable name and a degree it returns a polynomial for the indefinite integral, through a Taylor series where needed. With a list of the variable and two limits plus an accuracy it integrates numerically and returns the integral and an error estimate.
28s.stack: 'symb' 'name' n → 'symb''; 'symb' { name a b } x → integral error; «prog» { a b } x → integral error

≠.name: Not equal
≠.description: Tests two objects for inequality, returning 1 when they differ and 0 when they are equal; with names or algebraics it builds a symbolic comparison.

≤.name: Less than or equal
≤.description: Compares level 2 against level 1 and pushes 1 if it is smaller or equal, else 0; accepts reals, binary integers, strings and compatible units, and yields a symbolic comparison for names or algebraics.

28s.description: Compares level 2 against level 1 and pushes 1 if it is smaller or equal, else 0; accepts reals, binary integers and strings (compared by character code), and yields a symbolic comparison for names or algebraics.

≥.name: Greater than or equal
≥.description: Compares level 2 against level 1 and pushes 1 if it is larger or equal, else 0; accepts reals, binary integers, strings and compatible units, and yields a symbolic comparison for names or algebraics.

28s.description: Compares level 2 against level 1 and pushes 1 if it is larger or equal, else 0; accepts reals, binary integers and strings (compared by character code), and yields a symbolic comparison for names or algebraics.

▶.name: Infix store
▶.description: Infix form of storing a value in a variable, as produced by the store key in algebraic mode; the value is kept as the result.
